Correction: in gameplay, delta (fast) draws are not 0. The 'Fast draw per second: 0/1/79/223/304 delta' lines are the boot and menu windows (r49 49-59 s, r50 335-355 s; 100-2600 draws/s). In play, r49 reports 33,931-42,530 delta draws/s out of 90,762-110,896 draws/s (37-42%), and r50 reports 26,880-33,215 out of 84,905-90,114 (31-37%), e.g. r50 L4756/L4958 (vk_rasterizer.cpp:615/652/685).

Ineligible draws: indirect 1.8-2.8k/s, mesh 0.7-2.1k/s, and 1.4-4.1k/s from pipelines with 'computed handles'. Those are tuned4's handle-table pipelines, which #858's ComputedHandles blocker keeps out of both the memo and delta draws (HANDOFF round 18).

'State changed' by last break:
- register 27-34k/s
- deferred call 10-17k/s
- delta overflow 1.5-2.8k/s
- fence release 0.2-0.3k/s
- tick work ~25/s

Registers by method:
- 0x700, vertex_streams[0] word 0 (stride/enable): 7-15k/s; 0x73c (stream 15 word 0) 0.4-0.8k/s.
- 0x4da, blend.enable[2]: 3.2-4.5k/s.
- 0x460, 0x464, 0x466 (vertex_attrib_format): 2-5k/s, 0.3-0.7k/s, 0.4-0.9k/s.
- 0x853, pipelines[5].register_count, a real fragment program change: 1.8-2.9k/s.
- 0x64f, viewport_clip_control: 1.3-2.1k/s.
- 0x372, polygon_offset_fill_enable: 0.4-1.7k/s.
- 0x301, viewport[0].scale_y: 0.4-0.6k/s.
- 0x201, rt[0] address: 0.3-0.5k/s.
- 0x783 (blend_per_target) and 0x648 (cull face): ~0.3k/s each.

Code: Nx2FastDraw::Break bumps g_serial for every changed 3D register that isn't a fast-draw parameter (Maxwell3D::IsFastDrawParameter/IsFastDrawVertexBuffer/IsFastDrawDeltaMethod, maxwell_3d.cpp:356-443). In tuned4, IsFastDrawVertexBuffer accepts only words 1 and 2 of a stream (address), not word 0 (stride/enable) (maxwell_3d.cpp:414-420). Every Kind::Call without FastDrawNeutral breaks (gpu_split.cpp:773-776), and that includes the back-macro calls FrontRunOnBack defers (17.7k/s, the back's 'macro' zone count). Delta::MaxWrites = 16 CB write ranges per gap (nx2_fast_draw.h:133) overflows with Ocarina's ~5 CB uploads per draw.

What would enable more:
1. Upstream open PR #1216's last commit 9ad7c7cee (DjouWish, 2026-11-10; its other three commits are already in tuned4 as 9389e4f68/974469aa5/cf811c16a). Stride words become light when the device has extended dynamic state and VK_EXT_vertex_input_dynamic_state (g_dynamic_strides), the back-macro DeferWords calls become FastDrawNeutral, render_enable.address becomes a report operand, and fence-flagged short-query releases break again. That covers the two largest break reasons, ~20-30k/s of the ~42-53k. Check first that the RX 9070 XT driver exposes vertex_input_dynamic_state: the setting is true, but nothing in the log confirms the extension, so add a one-line log.
2. Raise Delta::MaxWrites to 64 (removes the 1.5-2.8k/s overflows).
3. Later, our own experiment: registers that only feed dynamic state UpdateDynamicStates sets on both paths (viewport transform, cull face, polygon offset enable with EDS2), gated per device feature and checked with EDEN_NX2_FAST_DRAW_VERIFY=1. Blend enable, attribute formats and clip control are in the pipeline key, so they must keep breaking unless the key excludes them.

Payoff: prepare time is 5.5-6.3 us for a full draw and 1.0-1.2 us for a delta draw ('prepare us per draw'). Each converted draw saves ~4.8 us. Moving 20-25% of ~2,100 draws per frame saves ~2-2.5 ms/frame; 1.5-2.5 ms is realistic.
zones.other_bucket:
'other' is not a measured zone. Report sets it to the window's wall time minus the sum of all zones (nx2_profile.h:522-528). It therefore holds every back-thread instruction outside a zone, plus any time the thread was descheduled outside a zone.

What it contains:
- GpuSplit::Execute's decode switch and per-entry overhead for ~110-135k ring entries per frame: the head decode, back_engine, the HasSegment/Direct/IsLast tests, the hook_requested and tick_requested loads, the 4096-word consumed.store(seq_cst) with NotifyFront (gpu_split.cpp:680-783, 864-893).
- Non-executable state writes that are not Direct: method_sink.emplace_back (gpu_split.cpp:729-730) and their later ConsumeSink/ConsumeSinkImpl, i.e. ProcessDirtyRegisters for each sunk write (maxwell_3d.cpp:327-354). This is outside every zone at level 1; the fine 'sink' zone covers it.
- Kind::Call bodies that open no zone (gpu_split.cpp:773-780): front-deferred report and DMA notes and similar calls.
- The idle hook Scheduler::FlushDeferred, which leads to Flush and SubmitExecution when the back runs dry (gpu_split.cpp:840-842 and 874-877; 2,213 submits/s in total).
- MaybeTick's tick hook GPU::TickWork for guest read flushes (gpu_split.h:738-744, RequestTick from GPU::OnCPURead, gpu.cpp:347-376).
- Preemption on the power-limited laptop (wall time, not CPU).
- The profiler's own Report and per-method counting.

How to split it, in order of cost:
1. Run once with EDEN_NX2_GPU_PROFILE=2 (no build needed). It adds the fine zones 'sink', 'macro end', 'tick work', 'cb bind', 'cb upload', 'query report', 'counter reset', 'render enable', 'draw setup', 'draw queries', 'geometry buffers' and 'storage bindings' (nx2_profile.h:84-98), and the uniform counters.
2. Add TEST zones, profile-only:
   - 'deferred call' around the Kind::Call body, with a top-N by function pointer as TopMethods does for methods;
   - 'idle hook' around both idle_hook() calls;
   - 'tick hook' inside MaybeTick when the exchange succeeds;
   - 'notify front' around NotifyFront when front_waiting is set;
   - a SampledScope 'ring dispatch' around Execute itself, with the 3D CallMethod's sampled time subtracted as a child.
3. Log the back's CPU time against its wall time over the same window (Common::CurrentThreadCpuTimeNs is already read in Report). other_cpu = (busy CPU − zoned time that was on CPU) is hard to get exactly, but wall − CPU − split-wait sleep gives the descheduled share.

Expect most of the 2.1-2.6 ms to be entry dispatch, sink consumption and the idle-hook submits. Those shrink with fewer entries (instance fold, CB fusion), not with micro-tuning.
zones.method_stream:
Numbers come from the 'GPU back thread methods per second' lines in gameplay windows (r49 12 windows, r50 12 windows; method counts above 2 M/s), divided by each window's fps. Script: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Lichii/e57b64ae-d8d0-5bc0-9be5-b5fd2191474e/scratchpad/bt-zones/methods.py.

Totals: methods per frame 113k (r49) and 135k (r50). The 3D register writes the profile counts number 88k and 99k per frame, of which 26.5k and 29.5k repeat the value. The top-24 list covers ~71%; the tail is mostly more CB data words (0x8e7-0x8f3) and assorted state.

All 3D (Maxwell3D), per frame in r50:
- CB select (const_buffer.size/address_high/address_low/offset, 0x8e0-0x8e3): 30.9k, 0 same. Per draw that is ~4.8 uploads (0x8e2 396k/s against ~82k draws/s).
- CB data (0x8e4-0x8f3): over 20.7k in the top-24 alone, 6.3k 'same'. Same here means equal to the previous word; it is still a memory write at an advancing offset, so it can't be dropped. Most uploads are 1-3 words: data[0] 382k/s, [1] 214k/s, [2] 114k/s.
- draw.begin (0x586): 10.1k, 9.95k same. These are the instance_id=Subsequent writes of an instance loop, ~6 per draw.end/draw.
- CB bind (bind_groups[n].raw_config, 0x904/0x914/0x91c/0x924): 8.8k, 1.8k same.
- vertex_id_base, global_base_vertex_index, global_base_instance_index (0x446/0x50d/0x50e): 7.1k, 0 same. Real per-draw parameters.
- index_buffer.count/first (0x5f8/0x5f7): 4.2k, 3.0k same.
- report_semaphore.query, clear_report_value, render_enable.mode (0x6c3/0x54c/0x556): 3.5k, all same. Executable per-draw query ops, fast-draw neutral.
- draw.end (0x585): 2.4k, all same. The General-mode ends that each issue a draw.
- MME DMA operands 0x154/0x155/0x158: 1.5k (17.7k/s, one per back macro).
- pipelines program registers (0x816/0x813/0x817/0x853...): ~0.7k.

So the back's 1.13 M/s of 'same value' writes are almost all executable methods. The front already drops same-value state registers before queueing: FrontWrite skips 5.46 M of its 9.28 M writes per second (maxwell_3d.cpp:1611-1619), plus #488's instance-loop store-only methods (1620-1633) and the instance-loop draw.end and vertex_buffer writes (FrontSkipsLoopWrite, 2486-2510). The earlier 'can the front drop 0x586?' question therefore needs per-method semantics, not a same-value test.

Where they can go:
1. Front, before queueing. Fold the later instances of an instance loop into one call: upstream open PR #1274's FoldInstance (57be5a6673: GpuSplit::FoldInstance/FlushFold before the next Reserve/Publish/Drain, DrawManager::AddLoopInstances, a FastDrawNeutral Defer, EDEN_NX2_FOLD_INSTANCES=0). That is ~9-10k entries per frame down to ~1-2k. The PR's list-draw/list-dispatch parts overlap tuned4's Nx2ListIndirect (#805 port) and need a separate review.
2. Front, our own design (no upstream PR does this). Fuse 'CB select (4 regs) + N data words' into one Call entry. It applies the final register values (with the same shadow-RAM Track/Replay handling and dirty flags), then WriteWordsCached, NoteFastDrawConstantData and the accumulator range once. That is ~50k methods per frame down to ~8k entries. It must keep CallConstBufferWords' page and size clipping (maxwell_3d.cpp:709-713) and the perf_verify path.
3. Front, small. Drop index_buffer.count when the front knows draw_indexed is already set inside an instance loop and no draw was issued since (~2k/frame). Drop a CB bind whose raw_config, address and size all match that slot's last bind (rare).
4. Back. Nothing large: state writes already take WriteStateRegister (maxwell_3d.cpp:582-591, unprofiled), and CB words are batched (gpu_split.cpp:697-723). Upstream #1095 (52d46375f) is largely in tuned4 already: WriteStateRegister, ProcessShadowRam and ProcessDirtyRegisters are inline in maxwell_3d.h:3339-3380. Only its EDEN_NX2_PERF_VERIFY-as-plain-flag part would add a little.
top_levers: 0. Measure before building: one run with EDEN_NX2_GPU_PROFILE=2 (no new build) to split 'method' into cb bind/cb upload/query report/render enable/sink and 'draw' into draw setup/draw queries/tick work. Also log whether the device has VK_EXT_vertex_input_dynamic_state, which decides lever 1. Profiled runs overstate 'method': CallMethod skips its WriteStateRegister shortcut under the profile (maxwell_3d.cpp:582-591).

1. More delta draws: port upstream open PR #1216's last commit 9ad7c7cee (stride words, back-macro calls and render-enable addresses keep fast draws), and raise Nx2FastDraw::Delta::MaxWrites from 16 to 64 (nx2_fast_draw.h:133). It targets the two largest break reasons (0x700 stride 7-15k/s, deferred calls 10-17k/s) and the 1.5-2.8k/s overflows. Full draws cost 5.5-6.3 us and delta draws 1.0-1.2 us. Estimate 1.5-2.5 ms/frame. Verify with EDEN_NX2_FAST_DRAW_VERIFY=1. Doesn't touch FSR 4, frame generation or the preparation stamp.

2. Fewer ring entries: upstream open PR #1274's instance folding (57be5a6673, FoldInstance/AddLoopInstances, EDEN_NX2_FOLD_INSTANCES) takes ~10k draw.begin per frame down to ~1-2k calls: 0.3-0.5 ms/frame on the back. Its list-draw/dispatch half could also cut the front's 'list writers' and 'list GPU wait' waits, but it overlaps our #805 Nx2ListIndirect and needs its own review.

3. Fuse each CB select+data run into one front entry (our own design; vet with EDEN_NX2_PERF_VERIFY and the maxwell_fast_method test): ~50k of ~120k methods per frame are const_buffer size/addr/offset plus 1-3 data words. Estimate 0.8-1.2 ms/frame on the back, less ring traffic on the front.

4. Bank check rewrite (our EXP9 port, CheckNativeBankPagesTracked buffer_cache.h:2940ff): plain loads before the two atomic Take() RMWs, a per-bank snapshot pointer cache instead of 16 unordered_map lookups per bind, and one mapped-size pass. 0.7-0.8 down to ~0.3 ms/frame. Also port upstream #1059 (a32f462aa, compare small UBOs in place) for the 1.45 ms uniform zone: ~0.2-0.3 ms.

5. Compute: 131-178 dispatches per frame at 16-22 us each (2.3-3.4 ms/frame) with no sub-zones. Add fine zones (lookup, configure, the TryOcarinaDlss FSR 4 replacement, record), then a dispatch memo for the repeated small dispatches. Estimate 0.5-1.5 ms. Keep the FSR 4 replacement path unchanged. Upstream #1246 is a small extra.

6. Fences: ~400 SignalFence per frame, and even a skipped one costs ~2 us in GPU::InvalidateGPUCache's gather (gpu.cpp:117-147). Return early when !Core::g_writes_collected, as AccelerateDMA already does (vk_rasterizer.cpp:4377); pool InnerFence; coalesce back-to-back query fences. Estimate 0.2-0.4 ms/frame.

7. Lock contention and per-draw locks: the back waits 17-82 ms/s on spin mutexes in r50 (15-30 ms/s in r49), i.e. 0.5-2 ms/frame inside zones. Fold MemoryManager::FlushCaching's InnerInvalidation (it takes buffer_cache.mutex per draw, vk_rasterizer.cpp:2812) into PrepareDraw's existing lock, add accumulator ranges per run rather than per word, and find the other holders (fence thread, async read-back readers). Estimate 0.3-0.8 ms/frame.

8. Back idle: the front's line shows 'publishes to an idle back late by 50.4 ms/s' (~1.3 ms/frame). Publish sooner when back_waiting/back_idle_at says the back is idle; part of the 2.4-2.9 ms split wait becomes overlap.
9. Hitches (1% lows, not the average): texture-cache collector Finish at texture_cache.h:219, 2-3.4 per second at 4-7 ms each. Look at upstream #1306 and #1311 and Fritchii EXP57.

Vetted but not first: Eglantine b1e650849e (per-thread GPU page translation cache, Fritchii EXP63 default off, ~3% of the back in kraibse's test) is low risk and worth an A/B after levers 1-4. Eglantine f27522bfb9 'hot pages' (Fritchii EXP48 default off) uploads a hot page at most once a frame, so a CPU write after its upload reaches the GPU a frame late: stale data within a frame, rejected under our correctness rule. Upstream #1088/#1245 (AMD 512-draw budget, batched uploads) and #974 are already in tuned4. Combined realistic total of levers 1-8: ~5-8 ms/frame, enough for the 5-6 ms the back must lose if most of it lands.

ideas.area:
Method processing on the GPU back thread. Measured in r50 at 452 s: 4.79 M method-zone entries/s, 153 ms/s, 40.5 fps, so about 118k entries and 3.8 ms per frame. Of these, 3.54 M/s are 3D register writes. Most of the rest (1.25 M/s) are not 3D: compute and other engine entries, each timed with a full Scope.

Estimated split of the 3D part per second. These are reasoned costs to confirm with EDEN_NX2_GPU_PROFILE=2:
- CB uploads: about 415k runs, 0.85 M words.
- CB select state writes (0x8e0-0x8e3): 1.08 M. These are Direct macro writes, about 10 ns each.
- draw.begin: 384k, 377k of them same-value instance-loop writes.
- CB binds: about 0.33 M.
- Per-draw query ops (0x6c3/0x54c/0x556): about 120k.
- Per-draw parameters (0x446/0x50d/0x50e): 0.28 M.

Two corrections to phase 1:
1. Profiling itself inflates the 'method' zone by about 0.8-1.3 ms/frame. Each counted 3D write pays about 5-8 ns, and each full Scope on a non-3D entry about 15-25 ns.
2. CB select+data fusion saves 0.3-0.5 ms standalone, not 0.8-1.0 ms. The CB write work itself stays.

The largest finding: our ring layout has real false sharing. The front writes write_position (offset 40) on every Commit. The back reads ring (offset 32) and system (offset 8) on every entry, and they are on the same 64-byte line. Probe: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Lichii/e57b64ae-d8d0-5bc0-9be5-b5fd2191474e/scratchpad/bt-method/off.cpp. Upstream #1251's layout commit fixes it.

A Fritchii finding is also relevant. Fritchii has shipped in-order state-pair blocks plus a front-side drop of same-value compute writes as built-in defaults since v5.5. The owner's Fritchii log counts them at 1.6-1.9 M pairs/s and 0.26-0.33 M dropped compute writes/s.

Realistic total for this area: about 1.2-2.4 ms/frame unprofiled. Some of these overlap.

ideas.title: 0. Fix the profile so 'method' measures what normal play pays (time non-3D entries by sampling, count entries per engine)
ideas.mechanism: These paths time each entry with a full Nx2Profile::Scope: non-3D Kind::Method and Kind::Multi entries (gpu_split.cpp:745, 751, 768), compute macro emits (kepler_compute.cpp:192) and back-macro 3D writes (macro.cpp:1422). A full Scope makes two rdtsc reads plus bookkeeping. The 3D path already uses SampledScope (maxwell_3d.cpp:599, 747). Switch these to SampledScope. Add one profile-only counter per entry kind on the back: 3D Direct, 3D sunk, 3D CB run, non-3D Method by engine, Multi, Call, Engine. Report them beside 'GPU back thread methods per second'. Unprofiled play gains nothing, but it shows how big the real target is. It also tells us what the 1.25 M/s non-3D entries are, which ideas 2 and 5 depend on.
ideas.expected_saving_ms: 0 ms in unprofiled play. In profiled runs it removes about 1.25 M/s × 15-25 ns = 19-31 ms/s, which is 0.45-0.77 ms/frame at 40.5 fps. Note that the 3D counting also costs about 3.54 M/s × 5-8 ns (CountRegisterWrite plus SampledScope bookkeeping) = 18-28 ms/s, or 0.4-0.7 ms/frame. So the unprofiled back is probably 0.8-1.3 ms/frame lighter than the 18.4/21.3 ms measured.
ideas.evidence: In r50 at 452 s, the 'method' zone counts 4,785,374/s and '3D register writes' 3,542,589/s. Both count every 3D write and CB word the same way (CountRegisterWrite plus SampledScope entries), so the 1.24 M/s difference is full-Scope entries. Scope (nx2_profile.h:244-280) subtracts no timing overhead; SampledScope does (TimingOverheadTicks, 375).
ideas.sources: Original. It follows the idea of upstream #1161 b964e6b40c ('profile the 3D methods on the path unprofiled runs take'), which tuned4 already has for 3D.
ideas.correctness_risks: None. Profile-only code behind Nx2Profile::Enabled().
ideas.how_to_measure: Compare the back's 'method' ms/s and 'other' ms/s before and after in the same save. Read the new per-kind counts. Then run once with EDEN_NX2_GPU_PROFILE=2 (no new build needed for the fine zones). Its 'cb upload', 'cb bind', 'query report', 'counter reset', 'render enable' and 'sink' zones split the remaining 3D cost and confirm the estimates for ideas 3, 4 and 6.

ideas.title: 1. Take the split ring's cache-line layout fix (upstream #1251, 5100362a6f)
ideas.expected_saving_ms: About 0.3-1.0 ms/frame. The back runs about 4.8 M entries/s while the front commits about 4 M entries/s. If 10-25% of back entries take a ~50 ns cross-core line transfer, that is 0.48-1.2 M × 50 ns = 24-60 ms/s, or 0.6-1.5 ms/frame at 40.5 fps. I take the lower half. The PR author measured about 3% fps, which is about 0.7 ms of our 24.7 ms frames.

That is about 3% on an i7-11700 with an RTX 3080, a small sample; the fixed-field pair agreed but its p99 was worse. Our offsets come from compiling gpu_split.h with offsetof (probe at /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Lichii/e57b64ae-d8d0-5bc0-9be5-b5fd2191474e/scratchpad/bt-method/off.cpp). ideas.how_to_measure: This can't be switched live, so package two builds in one round. Run the same save, same scene, three runs each. Compare the back's 'other' and 'method' ms/s, its host_cpu_busy_ms_per_s, fps and frame_times (debug server, frame_times seconds=30). Also compare the front's 'publishes to an idle back late by' line. In unprofiled play, read DKB frame_ms / 'Frame times' p50.

ideas.title: 2. Break fast draws for other engines at engine switches and on executable methods, not on every non-3D entry
ideas.expected_saving_ms: 0.05-0.25 ms/frame. Each skipped Break saves about 5-8 ns, the locked xadd plus the store-buffer drain on a store-heavy thread. Up to 1.25 M/s × 5-8 ns = 6-10 ms/s if most non-3D entries are plain or sunk, or 0.15-0.25 ms/frame at 40.5 fps. If only the about 0.35 M/s compute plain writes qualify (Fritchii's counts, idea 5), it is 0.05 ms/frame. Idea 0's counter decides which.
ideas.evidence: Code reading. The count of non-3D entries comes from r50 (4.79 M method entries/s minus 3.54 M 3D writes).
ideas.sources: Original
ideas.correctness_risks: A missed break lets a delta draw reuse bindings after other-engine work changed memory it reads: wrong textures or constants for one draw. The rule keeps a break on every executable method and on both engine switches, and plain compute stores touch no memory. Check with EDEN_NX2_FAST_DRAW_VERIFY=1 in Kokiri, the water and Castle Town.
ideas.how_to_measure: Watch the 'Fast draw state changes per second by last break' line: the other-engine count should fall, and full/delta draw counts shouldn't move. FAST_DRAW_VERIFY mismatches must stay at 0. The back's 'other' and 'method' ms/s should drop, and idea 0's per-kind counter shows how many breaks were skipped.

ideas.title: 3. Fold the later instances of instance loops on the front (upstream #1274, FoldInstance part only)
ideas.mechanism: The later instances of an instance loop arrive on the back as Direct draw.begin writes of the register's own value. Each one is a ring entry: Execute, CallMethod, CallMethodFast (maxwell_3d.cpp:627-636), ProcessShadowRam/ProcessDirtyRegisters, then DrawManager::DrawBegin, which only does instance_count++ (draw_manager.cpp:236-248). #1274 adds a check in FrontWrite: draw.begin, fs.instance_loop (tuned4 already tracks it, maxwell_3d.cpp:2466-2484), Subsequent, same value, !sink_pending, shadow_kept. On a match, the front counts instead of sending. GpuSplit::FoldInstance/FlushFold send the count before the next Reserve, Publish or Drain, as one FastDrawNeutral Defer of DrawManager::AddLoopInstances. Take only that part. The list-draw and list-dispatch halves (nx2_list_draw.h/nx2_list_dispatch.h) overlap our #805 Nx2ListIndirect and need their own review.
ideas.expected_saving_ms: 0.15-0.3 ms/frame on the back. r50 at 452 s has 0x586 at 384,469/s, 377,373/s of them same-value (9.3k per frame). Each costs about 15-20 ns in the handler plus about 5 ns of entry overhead: 377k × 20-25 ns = 7.5-9.5 ms/s. The folded calls cost about 1-1.5 ms/s, since loops number at most the ~85k draw.ends/s at ~15 ns each. Net about 6-8 ms/s, or 0.15-0.2 ms/frame at 40.5 fps, and about 0.25 ms in profiled runs. The front also saves about 377k Reserve/Commit/NoteWrites per second.
ideas.evidence: The method counts are from r50 L4267 ('0x586 384469/s (377373 same)'). The PR text: '~500,000 a second in Ocarina of Time'; it gives no fps number. Its unit test src/tests/video_core/instance_fold.cpp checks that folded instances draw what the writes draw.
ideas.sources: upstream open PR #1274 commit 57be5a6673 (DjouWish, 2026-11-10): maxwell_3d.cpp FrontWrite hunk, FlushFoldedInstances, DrawManager::AddLoopInstances, GpuSplit::FoldInstance/FlushFold.
ideas.correctness_risks: The fold must be flushed before anything else reaches the ring: every Reserve, Publish, Drain and WaitFor, and front reads such as FrontDmaRead. Otherwise the instance count lands after a later entry: a wrong instance count, or a draw issued too late. It also has to run in a defined order with our FrontSkipsLoopWrite and #488's same-value instance stores. Ship it unconditionally once verified; EDEN_NX2_FOLD_INSTANCES stays experiment-only.
ideas.how_to_measure: 0x586 should fall from about 384k/s to the loop count in 'GPU back thread methods per second'. The back's 'method' count and ms/s should drop by about 8 ms/s, and 'Instance fold per 2 s' (#1274's diag) should appear. A/B live with EDEN_NX2_FOLD_INSTANCES=0 during the test round. For correctness, compare screenshots of crowded instanced scenes (Kokiri grass, Castle Town crowd) and run with EDEN_NX2_PERF_VERIFY=1.

ideas.title: 4. Send runs of macro state writes as in-order pair blocks instead of one Direct entry each (structural)
ideas.mechanism:
Today every 3D macro state write the front doesn't drop is a Direct MacroWrite entry (FrontWrite, maxwell_3d.cpp:1672-1675; GpuSplit::MacroWrite, gpu_split.h:249-261). On the back each one runs Execute's decode, ConsumeSink and CallMethod's checks before WriteStateRegister (maxwell_3d.cpp:572-592), plus the BackLoop per-entry work (gpu_split.cpp:866-891).

The proposal: append such writes to an open block of (method, value) words, the same ring word size. The block stays open only until anything else is reserved or published, or the front waits; it never crosses the ring's end. The back applies a block in order, as ConsumeSinkImpl does: shadow RAM Track/Replay, same-value skip, ProcessDirtyRegisters while a deferred draw waits, then a tight loop that raises the two dirty tables at once (#717's ApplyFrontDelta).

Use in-order blocks only, never the deferred method sink (MACRO_SINK without RING_PAIRS). In tuned4, Kind::Call bodies run without ConsumeSink: back macros (FrontRunOnBack), Nx2ListIndirect calls and FinishFrontMacro. They would read stale registers if the writes waited in the sink.

CB select+data fusion (#717's FRONT_CB_ENCODE / Kind::CbWrite+CbBind) is a possible later add-on. After pair blocks it would save only about 0.1 ms/frame. Fritchii declined it because the front's macro DMA reads need each CB word's write noted at its own entry (c51c24f998 message), and our FrontDmaRead has the same constraint.
ideas.expected_saving_ms: 0.3-0.4 ms/frame unprofiled, 0.6-0.8 ms profiled. The owner's Fritchii v5.5 log (gameplay 1591-1671 s) shows 1.6-1.9 M pairs/s in 0.67-0.81 M blocks (2.3-2.4 per block), from 1.18-1.42 M/s macro state writes. Our r50 has the same stream: CB select 1.08 M/s plus 0x446/0x50d/0x50e 0.28 M/s and others. A Direct state write costs about 13-15 ns (5 ns entry, 8-10 ns dispatch); a pair in a block about 4-5 ns, plus about 5 ns per block. 1.8 M × 9 ns minus 0.77 M × 5 ns ≈ 12-15 ms/s, which is 0.3-0.37 ms/frame at 40.5 fps. Profiled runs also lose the per-write SampledScope and CountRegisterWrite cost (≈ 1.8 M × 6 ns = 11 ms/s). The front saves about 1 M Reserve/Commit per second, so it publishes sooner.
ideas.evidence: Fritchii ships EDEN_NX2_MACRO_SINK=1 and EDEN_NX2_RING_PAIRS=1 (with COMPUTE_SINK=1) as built-in defaults from v5.5 to v5.8.2 (refs/remotes/frizti/oot-gather-fix:src/yuzu/main.cpp:187-191). The owner played those builds. The counters are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Lichii/e57b64ae-d8d0-5bc0-9be5-b5fd2191474e/scratchpad/fritchii-log/eden_log.txt ('GPU split batched writes per second', e.g. L5284, L6260). Upstream #717 has the same design (Kind::StateDelta), but its fps gain (31 to 46 fps) covers the whole bundle, with no figure for this part. No isolated fps number for pairs exists anywhere.
ideas.sources: upstream open PR #717 eb3553bcb8 (Kind::StateDelta, Maxwell3D::ApplyFrontDelta with collected dirty flags; #641 4d1454a75c/2e5c8fad30). Fritchii 7853c03889 (EDEN_NX2_RING_PAIRS, 'Dr. Sergio', cherry-picked from d7dffbd85d), 516ba08ce5 (MACRO_SINK), 5c173ca274 (switches read at split start), and EXP22 c51c24f998/9638cca0ed (Fritchii's port of #641's delta onto RING_PAIRS, off by default). Port it in #717's shape with Fritchii's ordering rules.
ideas.correctness_risks: Ordering is the risk. A block must be closed before every other entry, Publish, Drain, WaitFor and engine switch, and before any front read that waits on positions (FrontDmaRead, acquires). Otherwise a Call or executable method runs before state written ahead of it: wrong state or a missed deferred-draw flush. The deferred-draw rule (ProcessDirtyRegisters flushes the instanced draw before the first non-loop write, maxwell_3d.h:3357-3360) must hold per pair, not per block. Don't merge rewrites of the same register within a block (EXP22's note: it changes dirty flags and deferred-draw flushes). Writes the front notes per entry (FrontNoteWrites) keep their positions, because a block's end position is where the back has run them all. Doesn't touch FSR 4, frame generation or the preparation stamp.
ideas.how_to_measure: Port Fritchii's 'GPU split batched writes per second' counters (pairs, pair_blocks). Expect pairs of about 1.3-1.9 M/s. The back's 'method' entries/s should fall by that amount, with lower 'method' and 'other' ms/s. Verify with EDEN_NX2_PERF_VERIFY=1 and EDEN_NX2_SPLIT_VERIFY=1 (front shadow check), plus an EXP22 bit 8-style check that applies each block both ways and compares registers and dirty flags (must stay 0). Run EDEN_NX2_FAST_DRAW_VERIFY=1 in Kokiri, the water and Castle Town.

ideas.title: 5. Drop same-value native compute plain writes on the front (Fritchii COMPUTE_SINK's same-value part)
ideas.expected_saving_ms: 0.1-0.12 ms/frame unprofiled, about 0.25 profiled. The owner's Fritchii v5.5 log counts 260-326k same-value compute writes dropped per second (compute_same) and 41-52k sunk. Each dropped entry saves about 12-15 ns on the back (entry, Break RMW, virtual call, store): 0.3 M × 13 ns ≈ 4 ms/s, or 0.1 ms/frame at 40.5 fps. Profiled runs also save the full Scope, 0.3 M × 20 ns = 6 ms/s. The front saves a similar amount.
ideas.evidence: Measured counts in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Lichii/e57b64ae-d8d0-5bc0-9be5-b5fd2191474e/scratchpad/fritchii-log/eden_log.txt, L5284-6863. Fritchii built-in default since v5.5 (EDEN_NX2_COMPUTE_SINK=1). Our r50 dispatch rate is similar (7.8k dispatches/s).
ideas.sources: Fritchii 516ba08ce5 (KeplerCompute::FrontPlainWrite, plain_sent, the SPLIT_VERIFY compute check), 4ddc1a058d (own switch) and 5c173ca274 (front copy of 0xb0 after inline QMD launches). Fritchii says they were cherry-picked from 284213c695 and 71a403f8bd by 'Dr. Sergio', which are not in any upstream Lichii PR we have.
ideas.correctness_risks: If the front copy differs from the back's while plain_sent is set, a needed write is dropped and the dispatch runs with a stale QMD field: wrong grid, shader or CB. Possible results are flicker, missing effects or a GPU fault. Port Fritchii's EDEN_NX2_SPLIT_VERIFY compute check (compare front and back registers every 4096 macro calls) and run it before shipping. Reset plain_sent on split start and stop, on QMD takeover and on every non-emit register path.
ideas.how_to_measure: Add Fritchii's compute_same and compute_sunk counters. Idea 0's non-3D entry count should fall by about 0.3 M/s. Watch the back's 'compute' ms/s for unchanged dispatch counts and 'method' ms/s for the drop. The SPLIT_VERIFY compute check must report 0 differences over a session through Kokiri, Hyrule Field and Castle Town.

ideas.title: 6. Cache the destination page of inline CB writes on the back
ideas.mechanism:
Each of about 415k CB uploads per second pays two costs.
- NoteFastDrawConstantData (maxwell_3d.cpp:1099-1134): the TIC/TSC range maths, two out-of-line DeviceSpans::Update calls (nx2_fast_draw.cpp:11-34), GpuToCpuAddress per 4 KiB page, two upper_bound Intersects and NoteDeviceData.
- WriteBlockImpl (memory_manager.cpp:587-650): Nx2BackSparseWrite's range check, the generic MemoryOperation page walk, finish_reads, then GetPointer and memcpy.

Ocarina writes its per-draw constants to consecutive offsets of a few buffers: address_low changes 415k/s, but mostly within the same page. Keep a one-entry cache on Maxwell3D: GPU page → device address, host pointer, big-page-continuous flag, and the 'page hits no header or sampler span' result. Key it on MemoryManager::MapSerial(), the tex_header/tex_sampler address and limit registers, and the DeviceSpans' own serial. On a hit: memcpy, accumulator.Add, NoteConstantData and NoteDeviceData. Still run the g_read_downloads/ReadDownloadsMayCover check (finish_reads) and the sparse range check on every write.
ideas.expected_saving_ms: 0.25-0.35 ms/frame. A hit saves about 25-35 ns of the about 60-80 ns per upload (≈ 15 ns of span/translation work in NoteFastDrawConstantData and ≈ 15-20 ns of MemoryOperation/GetPointer). 415k × 25-35 ns = 10-15 ms/s, or 0.25-0.36 ms/frame at 40.5 fps. The ceiling is the measured 'cb upload' fine zone.
ideas.evidence: Counts from r50 L4267 (0x8e2 address_low 414,859/s ≈ 0x8e4 data[0] 404,602/s, so one run per upload). Per-call costs are reasoned from the code. Kraibse measured a similar translation-only cache at the back thread going 13.64 to 13.25 ms/frame (Eglantine b1e650849e, via Fritchii EXP63 85a33019b). Ours is narrower and lands where most of the translation calls happen.
ideas.sources: Original. It is related to Eglantine b1e650849e / Fritchii EXP63 85a33019b (per-thread GPU page translation cache; don't copy its per-lookup getenv).
ideas.correctness_risks: A stale cached pointer after an unmap, remap or sparse mapping would write the wrong host memory or skip a texture-header break. The cache must be keyed on MapSerial (memory_manager.cpp:172, 236 bump it) and on the TIC/TSC registers, with the sparse and read-download checks kept per write. Check with EDEN_NX2_PERF_VERIFY=1 (CallConstBufferWords compares memory after the write, maxwell_3d.cpp:727-744) and EDEN_NX2_FAST_DRAW_VERIFY=1.
ideas.how_to_measure: Run EDEN_NX2_GPU_PROFILE=2 and read the 'cb upload' zone's ms/s and calls before and after (FineScope at maxwell_3d.cpp:750 and 1137). Add a profile-only hit/miss counter. Hits should exceed about 85%, and PERF_VERIFY must log no 'constant buffer words ... differs' lines.

ideas.area:
Compute dispatch on the GPU back thread: RasterizerVulkan::DispatchCompute (vk_rasterizer.cpp:2204-2424, zone opens at 2212) and ComputePipeline::Configure (vk_compute_pipeline.cpp:434-826). Baseline from the logs: about 150 dispatches per frame (r49 5.6-8.9k/s, r50 7.0-9.5k/s, at about 48 fps), 12-26 us each, 2.3-3.4 ms per frame. Outlier windows: r50 402 s at 73 us per dispatch, 442 s at 37 us, and the loading window at 362 s at 718 us. The 402 s window lines up with 152.5 MiB/s of host-memory staging in the 405.9 s SubmitCounts line. With oot_fsr_preset=Native (both logs), can_replace is true only for the 1440p upscale pass, so the FSR 4 path runs once per frame and is left unchanged. Upstream #1246's barrier is in tuned4 (dc31ee678a) and is recorded on the Vulkan worker, so it costs the back nothing.

Evidence for where the time goes: a least-squares fit over 11 r49 gameplay windows. Each window's compute ms/s was fitted against its dispatches/s and the per-window delta of the 'Native compute storage bindings ... of N bound' counter. That counter counts StorageBufferBinding cache misses, buffer_cache.h:4799-4823. Result: compute ms/s ≈ 12.2 us × dispatches/s + 5.6 us × misses/s. The correlation between misses per dispatch and us per dispatch is r = 0.67. Misses run at 1.9-8.5k/s, so 40-175 per frame. Script inline; the data is in r49log2/eden_log.txt. Repeated programs, from the DKB gpu_work lines: f8371c42621b1e57 runs 48-97 times per frame at 1x1x1, 6f9eacb79dad199c 15 times, eb1da88462fbae81 and 72edae24e28bfcf8 14 times each, 0a0bac9954d7f13e 2-6 times. So about 95-145 of the ~150 dispatches per frame come from five programs.

ideas.title: Measure first: compute sub-zones, binding counters and a slow-dispatch line (port Fritchii 753c422e13, plus three small counters)
ideas.expected_saving_ms: 0 directly. It decides between the items below. Their combined estimated range is 1.0-2.5 ms/frame out of the 2.3-3.4 ms; without the split, the 12.2 us per-dispatch base can't be attributed.
ideas.evidence: The compute zone has no sub-zones today (nx2_profile.h:39-107). The regression above ties about 5.6 us to each binding-cache miss but can't say which call pays it. Fritchii added exactly these counters on 2026-11-10, before its own EXP59 compute work (7df8caa2b8).
ideas.sources: Fritchii 753c422e13 (diagnostic only). Diagnostic tools stay in nx2 by our policy. The extra counters are original.
ideas.correctness_risks: None: everything sits behind EDEN_NX2_GPU_PROFILE / profile=2. Keep the extra timestamp reads FineScope so that profile=1 runs stay comparable.
ideas.how_to_measure: One run with EDEN_NX2_GPU_PROFILE=2 in Kokiri Forest and Castle Town. Read the new zones per dispatch, Query and binding misses per dispatch, and the pending-download length. Check that 'compute' plus the new sub-zones still adds up to today's 2.3-3.4 ms/frame.

ideas.title: Skip VirtualRangeCache::Query when the binding is one device-contiguous run (upstream #717 EDEN_NX2_BUFCACHE_CONTIG, made unconditional)
ideas.mechanism: UpdateComputeStorageBuffers (buffer_cache.h:3572-3582) calls ResolveMultiRangeStorage for every enabled SSBO on every dispatch (2858-2893), and graphics does the same at 3510. For read-only bindings this calls virtual_ranges.Query (virtual_range_cache.h:36). On a miss, Query walks every page with MemoryManager::GetSubmappedRange (virtual_range_cache.h:59). Since #1231 (in tuned4 as e8be28e5d6), read-only native compute and table pointers are bound to the end of their mapping, up to 1 GiB minus 64 KiB (buffer_cache.h:4768-4772). A new pointer near the start of a 130 MiB pool therefore walks about 2,000 64 KiB big pages, and a full 1 GiB reach walks 16k. StorageBufferBinding already clamps these bindings to MaxContinuousRange (4795), which answers from the device-contiguous runs kept at map time (memory_manager.cpp:728-752, merged only where the device addresses continue, 776-780). For such bindings Query can only return one segment, and the function then returns with segment_count 0. #717 tests `gpu_memory->MaxContinuousRange(binding.gpu_addr, binding.size) >= binding.size` before Query and returns early (#717 buffer_cache.h:1744-1748). Take it without the switch.
ideas.expected_saving_ms: r49 fit: about 5.6 us per binding-cache miss, at 1.9-8.5k misses/s (mean about 4k/s, about 85 per frame at 48 fps). That is 0.22-0.98 ms/frame tied to misses, about 0.48 on average. If the page walk is 50-80% of it: 0.15-0.75 ms/frame, typically about 0.3. Back-of-envelope for the miss mix: about 16% of misses are over 8 MiB ('reach past the old 8 MiB cap' 76.8k of 471.7k in r49), at about 2,000 pages × ~8 ns ≈ 17 us; the rest are ≤ 8 MiB, at ≤ 128 pages ≈ 1 us. That averages ≈ 3.6 us per miss, consistent with the fit. Graphics table-pointer binds save extra, not counted here.
ideas.evidence: Regression r = 0.67 between misses per dispatch and us per dispatch over 11 r49 windows. #717's comment: 'Native storage bindings are clamped to such a range, so Query only walked 8 MiB of pages for each new address'. With #1231 the clamp is now up to 1 GiB, so tuned4's walk is longer than the one #717 removed. Neither tuned4 nor Fritchii has the check (git grep finds no MaxContinuousRange(binding.gpu_addr ...)).
ideas.sources: Upstream open PR #717 (eb3553bcb8, nx2_bufcache.h g_contig_resolve; buffer_cache.h:1744-1748 on that head). Interacts with upstream #1231 (b6489bb5c7, already in tuned4).
ideas.correctness_risks: The outcome is identical when MaxContinuousRange is exact: one device run means Query would have found fewer than two segments. If the runs were stale after a remap, a multi-segment binding would bind as one range: wrong data, or a fault past a gap. The runs are rebuilt in Map/Unmap before map_serial bumps (memory_manager.cpp:170-172, 236). EDEN_NX2_PERF_VERIFY already compares MaxContinuousRange with the page walk (741-750).
ideas.how_to_measure: A/B the same spot (Kokiri, Castle Town) on profile=1: compute ms per dispatch, and refit it against the per-window delta of the 'Native compute storage bindings ... of N bound' line. The 5.6 us/miss term should drop toward about 1-2 us. With the item-1 counters: Query misses per second fall to near 0 for compute. Run EDEN_NX2_PERF_VERIFY=1 once: no 'Nx2Perf mapping runs' errors.

ideas.title: Fast-reject the pending-download walk in MarkWrittenBuffer, ClearFenceDownloads and OutdateReadDownloads
ideas.zone: compute (MarkWrittenBuffer per written SSBO and texel buffer; also draws and DMA)
ideas.mechanism: Every GPU write mark loops over all of pending_download_ranges, one RangeSet per fence with downloads not yet popped, and calls Subtract on each (buffer_cache.h:3604-3606). ClearFenceDownloads does the same (1482-1490), and OutdateReadDownloads walks every read_download's clean_ranges (904-919). RangeSet is pimpl'd (range_sets.inc:34ff), so each Subtract is an out-of-line call plus a binary search, even when the set is far from the address. Keep a [lower, upper) hull next to each deque entry, from the copies at CommitAsyncFlushesHigh (2200-2207; Subtract only shrinks a set, so the hull stays conservative). Skip entries the write misses, or keep one union RangeSet of all pending ranges and test Intersects first.
ideas.expected_saving_ms: N, the number of pending sets, ≈ fences with downloads per second × fence lifetime. r50 shows 3.8-21k download copies/s and about 12-14k fences/s. Assuming 3-8k download fences/s × 10-20 ms gives N ≈ 30-160. At 10-20 ns per Subtract that is 0.3-3 us per mark. With about 100-200 written compute bindings per frame (assumed about 1 per dispatch; item 1 counts it): 0.03-0.6 ms/frame, realistically 0.05-0.3, plus draw and DMA marks.
ideas.evidence: Reasoned from the code and the log rates. N is not logged today, so item 1's counter is the check. It costs nothing when N is small.
ideas.sources: Original. #717 left this loop as is (its MarkWrittenBuffer, 717 buffer_cache.h:2488-2499) and only guarded gpu_modified_ranges.Add (EDEN_NX2_BUFCACHE_MARK). That guard is a second small piece worth taking with it.
ideas.correctness_risks: Pure fast-reject: it skips only sets whose hull the write misses. An over-tight hull would let an old download overwrite a newer GPU result in guest memory (stale data), so build the hull from the copies actually recorded. EDEN_NX2_READ_CHECK=1 must keep 0 differing bytes.
ideas.how_to_measure: Item 1's counter (average N per mark). Then an A/B on profile=1: the compute zone per dispatch, and the 'fence' zone (CommitAsyncFlushes also walks committed sets). EDEN_NX2_READ_CHECK=1 for 2 minutes: 'Read download check' lines show 0 bytes differing.

ideas.title: Dispatch resolve memo, a 'delta dispatch' for repeated programs (structural)
ideas.expected_saving_ms: The fit's per-dispatch base is 12.2 us. If the resolve that a hit skips is about 40% of it (≈ 5 us; graphics' delta path removes about 80% of prepare), and 50-70% of the ~150 dispatches per frame hit (95-145 are repeats of five programs), that is 75-105 × 5 us ≈ 0.4-0.5 ms/frame. Skipping the lookup and rebuilding the bind lambda too gives up to ≈ 8 us × 100 ≈ 0.8 ms. Range 0.4-0.8 ms/frame.
ideas.evidence: The gpu_work lines show the repetition (f8371c42621b1e57 at 48-97 per frame, 1x1x1), and the fast-draw numbers show what skipping the resolve buys. Not measured for compute yet. First add a profile counter: 'dispatch whose memo key matches the last dispatch of the same pipeline'.
ideas.sources: Original for compute. Modeled on upstream #805/#974's delta draws (in tuned4) and #717's EDEN_NX2_STORAGE_MEMO, which reuses unchanged storage bindings (717 buffer_cache.h:2281).
ideas.how_to_measure: Profile=1: compute ms ÷ count before and after. A new profile-only 'dispatch memo hits/misses by reason' line. Run EDEN_NX2_DISPATCH_MEMO_VERIFY=1 (0 mismatches) over a 5-minute route.

ideas.title: Return NativeImageHandles by reference (upstream #1161 0593fd75f4)
ideas.mechanism: DispatchNativeCompute calls NativeImageHandles(regs.code_loc.Address()) for every Ocarina dispatch with CB0 enabled (kepler_compute.cpp:693, and 1274 in RememberNativeUpscaleInput). It returns std::pair<std::vector<u32>, std::vector<u32>> by value from its memo (1236-1240), which costs two vector copies, each a heap allocation and a free. Return a const reference into the unordered_map memo; references stay valid as the map grows.
ideas.expected_saving_ms: 4 heap operations at ~50-100 ns each ≈ 0.2-0.4 us per dispatch. × ~100-150 Ocarina dispatches with CB0 per frame ≈ 0.02-0.06 ms/frame.
ideas.evidence: The commit message: 'DispatchNativeCompute asks for every Ocarina of Time dispatch with constant buffer 0 (~4,700 a second in the field): two vector copies, each a heap allocation and free, on the split back.'
ideas.sources: Upstream open PR #1161, commit 0593fd75f4 (a cherry-pick of upstream 5edee0ccf); 7 lines in kepler_compute.cpp/.h.
ideas.correctness_risks: None, as long as nothing erases from the static memo while a reference is held; it is only ever inserted into.
ideas.how_to_measure: Hard to see on its own (within noise of the method zone). Take it with the other quick wins and check that 'method' ms/s doesn't rise.

ideas.title: Compute uniform-buffer reuse: memo the CB binding, rebind identical stream bytes (upstream #717 EDEN_NX2_COMPUTE_BINDCACHE)
ideas.mechanism:
Every dispatch:
- runs GpuToCpuAddress and FindBuffer for each enabled CB (buffer_cache.h:3554-3569);
- then streams it: BindMappedUniformBuffer plus ReadBlockUnsafe of the CB's used size, then Nx2PatchComputeUniform (3149-3212).

#717 memos the CB range to its Binding per slot (717 buffer_cache.h:2436-2456, ReuseGeometry/StoreGeometry). It also rebinds the previous stream allocation when the bytes are the same, via BindSmallUniformReusing with stage slot 5 (717 1945-1955). tuned4 already has that helper for graphics (uniform_stream_reuse.h:103; used at buffer_cache.h:2788), so the compute half is a small adaptation. Reuse only when Nx2PatchComputeUniform has nothing to patch, or compare after patching.
ideas.expected_saving_ms: About 0.2-0.5 us per dispatch (an address translation, a FindBuffer and a stream allocation, or more for larger CB0s) × ~150 = 0.03-0.08 ms/frame. It is more where CB0 repeats between the 60 1x1x1 dispatches of f8371c42621b1e57.
ideas.evidence: Graphics' version (upstream #1059 in tuned4: 27.6 to 8.9 ns for an unchanged 256 B bind). For compute, #717 gives no per-switch number (only the whole bundle: 31 to 46 fps).
ideas.sources: Upstream open PR #717 (eb3553bcb8). The helper comes from upstream #1059, already in tuned4.
ideas.correctness_risks: Rebinding is only valid within the same command buffer and stream generation (BindSmallUniformReusing already checks this for graphics). A GPU-modified CB must keep taking the cached path (the IsRegionGpuModified test at 3175-3178 stays first). The Nx2 list-word patching must not be skipped.
ideas.how_to_measure: Profile=2 'uniform rebinds' (FineCounter) rising for compute; compute ms per dispatch A/B.

ideas.title: Rate-limit the per-dispatch early-download landing check (MasterSemaphore::Refresh)
ideas.mechanism: After every dispatch, NoteWorkRecorded(true) (buffer_cache.h:942-956) calls RecordEarlyDownloads and, whenever pending_early_downloads != 0, runtime.IsFreeNow(front tick). That calls MasterSemaphore::Refresh, a vkGetSemaphoreCounterValue driver call (vk_master_semaphore.cpp:62-78, vk_buffer_cache.cpp:553-562), once per dispatch. Draws already check every 32nd time only. Check after a dispatch only when scheduler.CurrentTick() moved since the last check, or every 4th dispatch.
ideas.expected_saving_ms: 0.3-1 us per driver call (assumed for AMD on Windows) × up to ~150 dispatches/frame × the share with early downloads pending (preflush is on for Ocarina) ≈ 0-0.15 ms/frame.
ideas.evidence: Code reading only. The early downloads come from our preflush and async read-back, so the item-1 counter will show how often this runs.
ideas.sources: Original (tuned4's own preflush and async read-back code).
ideas.correctness_risks: Early downloads land in guest memory a little later. A read that needs them still waits through WriteFinishedReadDownloads or a flush, so the cost is at worst a few more on-demand flushes. No stale data, because landing order is unchanged.
ideas.how_to_measure: Item-1 Refresh counter before and after. 'Async read-back per second' and the 'GPU waits' lines must not rise. EDEN_NX2_READ_CHECK=1 stays at 0.

ideas.title: Defer the list-copy submit after a dispatch (upstream #717 DISPATCH_BATCH, ported by Fritchii as EXP27 bit 8)
ideas.mechanism: Every dispatch whose writes reach a command-list page ends with SubmitNx2ListCopies, a full scheduler.Flush() right away (vk_rasterizer.cpp:2470-2476, called at 2331/2354/2409). #717's DISPATCH_BATCH, ported as Fritchii 6de2b2739f bit 8, submits those copies only when the front waits for them (WaitSubmittedTick asks the back), when the back goes idle, or with the next submission (Scheduler::DeferFlushUntilWanted).
ideas.expected_saving_ms: Count unknown. r50 shows 2,200 submits/s (about 46 per frame) and 655 list-indirect dispatches/s of 0xe74. If about 5-15 flushes per frame come from here, at about 5-15 us each on the back: 0.03-0.2 ms/frame. Fewer AMD submissions also saves GPU-side time (the AMD 512-draw budget note at vk_rasterizer.cpp:4333-4336).
ideas.evidence: Code reading. Fritchii keeps it off by default and gives no number. Needs item 1's counter (and Fritchii 753c422e13's 'Submits per second by site').
ideas.sources: Upstream open PR #717 (EDEN_NX2_DISPATCH_BATCH); Fritchii 6de2b2739f (EXP27 & 8, off).
ideas.correctness_risks: If the front waits for a copy that no path submits, it waits longer ('list GPU wait' / 'list submit wait'), up to a stall until the next submit. The data stays correct (the copy is still ordered after the dispatch). Take it only if the counter shows the flushes are frequent.
ideas.how_to_measure: The submits-by-site counter before and after. The front's 'list GPU wait' and 'list submit wait' zones and the back's 'other' (idle-hook submits) must not grow.

ideas.title: Top-level dirty bitmap in the memory tracker, so a sync over a 1 GiB read-only binding visits only dirty 4 MiB regions (structural)
ideas.zone: compute (BindHostComputeStorageBuffers SynchronizeBuffer); also graphics table pointers
ideas.mechanism: SynchronizeBuffer (buffer_cache.h:4230ff) uses ForEachDirtyUploadRange (memory_tracker_base.h:193-205). It calls IteratePages<true>, which visits every 4 MiB manager of the range, creates the missing ones, and asks each for DirtyWords. A #1231 read-only native binding of up to 1 GiB is 256 managers per sync per dispatch. Keep a bitset with one bit per 4 MiB region, set wherever a manager gains a CPU-dirty or untracked word, and walk its set bits with countr_zero: 4 u64 words for 1 GiB. #717's SYNC_SKIP/SKIP_REGIONS (256 KiB-region generations, 717 buffer_cache.h:2987) is a heavier form of the same idea.
ideas.expected_saving_ms: 256 managers × ~5-10 ns ≈ 1.3-2.5 us per 1 GiB binding sync, ≈ 0.2-0.4 us for a 130 MiB one. The number of long bindings per dispatch is unknown (item 1's 'storage bytes bound'). At 0.5-1 long binding per dispatch × 150: 0.1-0.4 ms/frame.
ideas.evidence: Code reading. The long bindings exist ('reach past the old 8 MiB cap' is 16-26% of computed bindings in r49 and r50). The per-dispatch hit traffic is not logged yet.
ideas.sources: Original. Related: #717 EDEN_NX2_SYNC_SKIP/SKIP_REGIONS (off-by-default style switches, high risk as a bundle); Fritchii EXP59 & 4 (7df8caa2b8) does the per-word version for compute only, and tuned4 already has that by default (skip_clean at 4233).
ideas.correctness_risks: A path that makes words dirty without setting the region bit means a missed upload, so the compute shader reads stale input. Every ChangeRegionState(CPU/Untracked, true) and CachedCpuWrite flush must set it. EDEN_NX2_PERF_VERIFY's CleanWordsHold (memory_tracker_base.h:208-217) can be extended to check the bitmap too.
ideas.how_to_measure: Profile=2 'compute synchronize' zone per dispatch (from item 1) before and after. EDEN_NX2_PERF_VERIFY=1 shows no 'clean tracker words wrong' errors. FrameDump of the grass, fog and light-probe passes matches.

ideas.area: Per-draw work on the GPU back thread, and the fast (delta) draw path. In r50 gameplay (window at 422-426 s, 92-97k draws/s) the per-draw zones add up to about 398 ms/s: draw 51.5, flush work 27.0, pipeline lookup 17.7, configure 29.4, sync descriptors 2.7, read handles 33.1, fill image views 20.4, update buffers 48.7, bind stage buffers 5.2, uniform buffers 71.5, bank check 36.3, storage buffers 17.5, push descriptors 9.9, render targets 7.7, configure draw 4.4, dynamic state 11.4, draw record 2.3. That is 4.1 us per draw, about 8 ms per game frame at ~2,000 draws per frame (~47 game frames/s), so it is the largest single block on the back. ReportFastDraws in the same window: 30,854 delta draws/s and about 61,800 full draws/s. Full draws: 46,855 'state changed', 5,669 'handle data written', 3,859 'pipeline takes no delta draws' (computed handles), 3,135 'after an ineligible draw', 2,234 'different kind'. Prepare time is 5.63 us for a full draw and 1.08 us for a delta draw, so each full draw converted to a delta draw saves about 4.55 us. Last breaks behind 'state changed': register 29,755/s (0x700 13,184, 0x460 3,998, 0x4da 3,583, 0x853 2,029, 0x64f 1,472, 0x466 762, 0x464 548, 0x73c 490, 0x301 442, 0x465 379, 0x201 367, 0x783 336), deferred call 14,513, delta overflow 2,335, fence release 226. Device facts from the r50 log: dyna_state is EDS2 (the default, settings.h:823-832), so EDS3 blending is off (vulkan_device.cpp:742-768). vertex_input_dynamic_state is true, and the log says 'Vertex repacking without dynamic vertex input disabled'. All estimates below convert per-second rates at 47 frames/s and assume that only part of each 'last break' converts, because an earlier break in the same gap can still force a full draw. I measured nothing; idea 2 measures that conversion rate exactly.

ideas.title: Port upstream #1216's last commit 9ad7c7cee: vertex stride words, render enable addresses and back-macro calls no longer end fast draws
ideas.zone: fast-draw full path (draw, pipeline lookup, configure, read handles, fill image views, uniform buffers, bank check)
ideas.mechanism:
tuned4 already has #974's three commits (9389e4f68/974469aa5/cf811c16a); this fourth one is missing. Hunks against tuned4:
(a) Maxwell3D::IsFastDrawVertexBuffer (maxwell_3d.cpp:414-421) accepts word 0 of a stream (stride and enable) when Nx2FastDraw::g_dynamic_strides is set. That needs a new inline atomic in nx2_fast_draw.h, set in the RasterizerVulkan constructor (~vk_rasterizer.cpp:435). Why this is safe: with extended dynamic state the pipeline key holds strides only when EDS is off (fixed_pipeline_state.cpp:247-251). The stream enable bit is not in the key. ConfigureDelta still runs UpdateGraphicsBuffers and BindHostGeometryBuffers (vk_graphics_pipeline.cpp:1181-1184). UpdateDynamicStates and UpdateVertexInput run on both paths (vk_rasterizer.cpp:1127-1130, 4533-4540).
(b) render_enable.address_high/low become report operands (maxwell_3d.cpp:395-412).
(c) DeferWords (gpu_split.h:281) gains Defer's flags argument. The back-macro call in FrontRunOnBack (maxwell_3d.cpp:2183-2197) passes FastDrawNeutral, so gpu_split.cpp:776-779 no longer breaks with Reason::Call. Safe because the macro's own writes go through maxwell3d.CallMethod (macro.cpp:1421-1424) and ProcessDirtyRegisters (maxwell_3d.h:3357-3366), which break for any changed non-parameter register. The native path of MacroEngine::Execute has no unconditional break; only the non-native macro_cache path at macro.cpp:1645-1647 does.
(d) A fence-flagged short-query release ends the chain again (maxwell_3d.cpp:445-449). This tightens correctness.
Keep our Writes::Caches argument instead of upstream's Writes::Anywhere. I would derive g_dynamic_strides from the pipeline cache's dynamic_features.has_dynamic_vertex_input (vk_pipeline_cache.cpp:827-829, which includes the setting) rather than from the device alone, so it follows the same switch the pipelines use.
ideas.expected_saving_ms: 1.2-1.9 ms/frame. Breaks targeted (r50 at 426 s): deferred call 14,513 + 0x700 13,184 + 0x73c 490 = 28,187/s, i.e. ~600 draws/frame at 47 fps. Upper bound: 600 x 4.55 us = 2.7 ms/frame. With 45-70% converting (other breaks in the same gap), that is 270-420 draws x 4.55 us = 1.2-1.9 ms.
ideas.evidence: #1161's version of the deferred-call part (7824123e5) reports these were 'the last break before about 29,500 full draws a second' at Kokiri water. Our own log has back macros at 17.7k/s, against 12-14.5k/s 'deferred call' breaks, so nearly all deferred-call breaks are back macros.
ideas.sources: Upstream open PR #1216, commit 9ad7c7cee (DjouWish, 2026-11-10); same idea as #1161 7824123e5.
ideas.correctness_risks: A missed break means the delta draw keeps a stale pipeline or binding. Stride and enable are rebound on both paths, so the remaining risk is a pipeline without dynamic vertex input that repacks vertices. Such draws are already ineligible (NoteResolvedDraw: AnyVertexRepacked, vk_rasterizer.cpp:566), and with VIDS on repacking is disabled. A back macro whose effect bypasses CallMethod would be missed; the native interpreter's emit path does not bypass it. FSR 4, frame generation and the preparation stamp are not touched.
ideas.how_to_measure: Same spots (Kokiri water, Castle Town) with EDEN_NX2_GPU_PROFILE=1. Expect a ReportFastDraws 'delta' rate well above 30k/s, the 'deferred call' and 0x700/0x73c entries gone from 'by last break', 'prepare us per draw: all' down from 4.1 toward 3.2, and the back thread's pipeline lookup, read handles and fill image views counts down. Then a separate correctness run with EDEN_NX2_FAST_DRAW_VERIFY=1 plus EDEN_NX2_BACK_MACRO_VERIFY: the 'Fast draw verify per second' mismatch counts must be 0. Verify runs resolve every candidate in full, so they are not perf runs.

ideas.title: Cheap counter: which breaks a full draw had, not only the last one, plus a one-line log of g_dynamic_strides and VIDS
ideas.mechanism:
ReportFastDraws counts only g_last_break (vk_rasterizer.cpp:479-485, 664-685). A gap broken by 0x4da and then 0x700 shows only 0x700, so no lever's real yield is known. Add a bitmask of break classes to nx2_fast_draw.h: OR it into a std::atomic<u32> (relaxed) in Break, and only when the profile is on.
Classes:
- stride word
- attribute format (0x458-0x477)
- blend (0x4d8-0x4df, 0x780-0x7bf)
- program (pipelines[] 0x800-0x85f)
- viewport/scissor
- render target
- other register
- back-macro call
- other call
- delta overflow
- fence
- tick work, invalidation, map and texture headers
In TakeReusableDraw, on StateChanged, increment a small histogram indexed by the mask; clear the mask in NoteResolvedDraw. Log the top 12 masks every 10 s next to the existing lines. Also split 'different kind' into indexed/non-indexed, topology, indirect and inline index. For other calls, record the breaking entry's thunk pointer (entry[1], gpu_split.cpp:773-779) and log it module-relative, so the PDB can name the Defer site. Log once at boot whether EDS, VIDS and g_dynamic_strides are on (the r50 log confirms VIDS only indirectly).
ideas.expected_saving_ms: 0 by itself. It turns the 45-70% conversion guesses for ideas 1, 3, 6 and 8 into exact draws/frame: for example, draws whose mask is a subset of {stride, back-macro call} are exactly what idea 1 converts.
ideas.evidence: In the r50 data the 'by last break' sums equal 'state changed' (29,755+14,513+2,335+226+24 = 46,853 against 46,855/s). The counter is exact for the last break and blind to the others.
ideas.sources: Original; it extends #974's ReportFastDraws. A diagnostic, so it stays in nx2 off unless the profile is set, per AGENTS.md.
ideas.correctness_risks: None. Profile-only. A relaxed fetch_or on ~50k breaks/s costs about 1 ms/s, and only in profiled runs.
ideas.how_to_measure: One EDEN_NX2_GPU_PROFILE=1 run on the current build plus this counter, before porting ideas 1 and 3. The top masks give the conversion rate per lever.

ideas.title: Port #1161 792e12a47's fast-draw half: widen instead of overflow, attribute formats as draw parameters (type classes compared), handle checks per word
ideas.zone: fast-draw full path; breaks: delta overflow, vertex_attrib_format 0x460-0x466, 'handle data written'
ideas.mechanism:
Three parts of 792e12a47 (Lucas Borges), taken without its reports and fences half:
(1) AppendRange (nx2_fast_draw.h:159-172) merges a range into one it overlaps. When the list is full it widens the range that grows least, instead of NoteConstantData/NoteDeviceData calling Break(Reason::DeltaOverflow) (nx2_fast_draw.h:180-200). In tuned4 a widened range only makes Delta::Reaches and UniformRangeKept (buffer_cache.h:1838-1849) more conservative, since both are overlap tests. #1161 also disables uniform keeps when ranges widen; keep that for parity. Do not just raise MaxWrites to 64, as the zone diagnosis suggests. TakeReusableDraw copies Delta three times per draw (std::exchange plus taken_delta = delta, vk_rasterizer.cpp:464-466). At 16 entries that is ~0.55 KB each; at 64 it would be ~2.1 KB each, ~6.4 KB of memcpy/memset per draw: ~0.2-0.3 us x 2,000 = 0.4-0.6 ms/frame, more than the overflows cost.
(2) With dynamic vertex input, vertex_attrib_format writes become parameters. The delta draw then refreshes the pipeline key's attribute_types (fixed_pipeline_state.cpp:198-217) and compares it with the pipeline's; a different class takes the full path. UpdateVertexInput already resends the formats on both paths (the VertexInput dirty flag, vk_state_tracker.cpp:213).
(3) TakeReusableDraw's handle check (vk_rasterizer.cpp:503-519, Delta::Reaches) compares only the words handles are read from (Delta::ReachesWords), not the whole constant buffer. Ocarina writes ~5 CB uploads per draw into buffers that also hold handles.
ideas.evidence: The commit text names these exact break causes at Ocarina's water, but gives no timing. Our counts are from the r50 ReportFastDraws lines (L3751-3753).
ideas.sources: Upstream open PR #1161, commit 792e12a47 (fast-draw half only; overlaps #1216's stride part, so take #1216 first).
ideas.correctness_risks: (2): a format change within the same type class keeps the pipeline. That is only correct if UpdateVertexInput resends the new formats on the delta path, which needs the VertexInput dirty flag to stay set until then. (3): handle words must include the secondary (separate sampler) handle and the computed-handle inputs. A wrong word list gives wrong textures. Check with EDEN_NX2_FAST_DRAW_VERIFY=1 and EDEN_NX2_DELTA_DESCRIPTORS_VERIFY.
ideas.how_to_measure: In ReportFastDraws: 'delta overflow' gone from 'by last break', the 0x460-0x466 entries gone, 'handle data written' down, the delta rate up, 'prepare us per draw: delta' about the same. Verify-run mismatch counts must be 0.

ideas.title: Per-draw micro trims: Delta copies, the double buffer-cache lock, Ocarina trackers
ideas.zone: draw (0.58-0.61 us exclusive per draw), flush work (0.28-0.39 us per draw)
ideas.mechanism:
(a) Delta copies: TakeReusableDraw zero-fills and copies the whole Delta three times per draw (vk_rasterizer.cpp:464-466; struct at nx2_fast_draw.h:121-135, ~0.55 KB). Copy only the num_writes/num_device_writes used entries into taken_delta, and reset g_delta's counts and binds instead of assigning Delta{}.
(b) Double lock: PrepareDraw's FlushWork zone calls gpu_memory->FlushCaching() (vk_rasterizer.cpp:815-818). On most draws InvalidateAll yields the inline CB ranges, and InnerInvalidation (vk_rasterizer.cpp:2790-2826) takes buffer_cache.mutex (a SpinRecursiveMutex) to run WriteMemory. About 1 us later, PrepareDraw takes buffer_cache.mutex and texture_cache.mutex together (vk_rasterizer.cpp:1035). Move FlushCaching to just after that scoped_lock and before draw_serial and draw_map_serial are read (1038-1039). The recursive spin lock then only counts, and a break FlushCaching causes (Invalidation) is still seen by DeltaStillHolds. That is one lock round trip less per draw, and one window less where the fence thread or async read-back can contend (the back waited 22.6-70 ms/s on spin mutexes in r50).
(c) Ocarina trackers: OcarinaDlssEnabled() (vk_rasterizer.cpp:3248-3277) runs 2-3 times per draw, from TrackOcarinaCamera, TrackOcarinaActor and the final-pass check (1099-1101, 1152). Each call does a function-static guard, settings reads, call_once and an atomic. Latch the result once per render_trace_frame. Put a FineScope around the two trackers to measure them. TrackOcarinaActor copies up to sizeof(pose.bones) (~13 KB) per skinned draw (vk_rasterizer.cpp:3545-3549). Keep their behaviour; they feed FSR 4 and frame generation motion.
ideas.expected_saving_ms: 0.2-0.4 ms/frame. (a) 2,000 draws x 40-60 ns = 0.08-0.12 ms. (b) 2,000 x 30-60 ns uncontended = 0.06-0.12 ms, more when contended. (c) 2,000 x 2-3 calls x 10-15 ns = 0.04-0.09 ms, plus whatever the tracker zone shows for skinned draws.
ideas.evidence: Reasoned from the code and the measured per-draw costs: 'draw' is 51.5 ms/s over 95k draws/s, 'flush work' is 27.0 ms/s over 97k/s, and this thread's spin contention is 764/s for 22.6 ms/s.
ideas.sources: Original (code review of tuned4). (b) follows the zone diagnosis's lever 7.
ideas.correctness_risks: (b): FlushCaching must stay before draw_serial is read, and before TakeReusableDraw's result is trusted; DeltaStillHolds already re-checks the serial under the lock. (c): a latched FSR state could be one frame late after an FSR failure, and TryOcarinaDlss checks separately. FSR 4 and frame generation are otherwise unaffected.
ideas.how_to_measure: EDEN_NX2_GPU_PROFILE=1: the 'draw' and 'flush work' ms per call, and 'prepare us per draw' for both paths. Spin mutex contention: the 'this thread' line. EDEN_NX2_GPU_PROFILE=2 with the new tracker FineScope.

ideas.title: Structural: delta draws with a pipeline lookup after register-only breaks (same pipeline, nothing changed that resolves textures)
ideas.zone: fast-draw full path after the 'register' breaks that remain once ideas 1 and 3 are in
ideas.mechanism:
Today any changed non-parameter register bumps g_serial (maxwell_3d.h:3361-3364). The next draw then does everything again: pipeline lookup, handle reads, image views, samplers, and no uniform keeps (BeginGraphicsUniforms(nullptr), vk_rasterizer.cpp:1057). Change it as follows.
- Add a second serial that only breaks which can change texture or descriptor resolution bump: tex_header and tex_sampler pool registers, sampler_binding, the bindless texture CB slot, texture header data, invalidation, map, fence, tick work, and calls that are not FastDrawNeutral. Delta methods already track CB binds and handle data.
- In TakeReusableDraw on StateChanged: if that serial is unchanged, do the normal PipelineLookup. If it returns draw.pipeline (and the bound pipeline, render pass and tick checks still hold), take the ConfigureDelta path: kept descriptors, uniform keeps, no handle reads or FillImageViews.
- The real lookup proves the pipeline key, so no per-register whitelist is needed. The second serial proves the textures. Dynamic-only registers (viewport 0x301, scissor, depth bias, stencil refs) are covered because UpdateDynamicStates and UpdateRenderTargets run on both paths (vk_graphics_pipeline.cpp:1266-1274; vk_rasterizer.cpp:1127-1130). A render target change (0x201) still breaks the render pass check.
ideas.expected_saving_ms: 0.4-1.0 ms/frame after ideas 1 and 3. Remaining register last-breaks: 29,755/s minus stride (13.7k) minus attribute formats (5.7k) ≈ 10k/s ≈ 215 draws/frame. Program changes (0x853, ~2k/s) and blend/clip-control key changes under EDS2 (0x4da, 0x783, 0x64f, ~5.4k/s) look up a different pipeline and gain nothing. If 30-60% keep the same pipeline, 65-130 draws x ~4.2 us (4.55 minus the 0.28 us lookup kept) = 0.3-0.55 ms. Up to ~1 ms if idea 2 shows many gaps whose only breaks are dynamic-state registers.
ideas.evidence: Reasoned. The delta path's 1.08 us against the full path's 5.63 us is measured. The same-pipeline fraction is unknown until idea 2's counter runs.
ideas.sources: Original; generalizes the zone diagnosis's lever 3 (dynamic-state registers as parameters) without a hand list of dynamic-only registers.
ideas.correctness_risks: Wrong textures or samplers if a texture-relevant register is missing from the second serial: list them from the texture cache's and GraphicsPipeline::Configure's register reads. Rescaling and scale epoch are already checked (kept_scale_epoch, vk_graphics_pipeline.cpp:1194). Storage buffer bindings are redone on the delta path. EDEN_NX2_FAST_DRAW_VERIFY must cover the new case: resolve in full and compare views, samplers and kept bindings, as now.
ideas.how_to_measure: Add a 'delta after lookup' count to ReportFastDraws. Expected: 'state changed' falls by that count, prepare us 'all' drops, and the pipeline lookup count stays about the same. Verify runs: mismatches 0. A/B at Castle Town and Kokiri water with EDEN_NX2_GPU_PROFILE=1.

ideas.title: Delta draws for pipelines with computed texture handles (#1161 e05a72847)
ideas.zone: fast-draw 'pipeline takes no delta draws: computed handles'
ideas.mechanism: tuned4 blocks every pipeline whose texture, image or buffer descriptors have a handle_program, with DeltaBlocker::ComputedHandles (vk_graphics_pipeline.cpp:455-485). These are our handle-table pipelines, kept out by #858's blocker. e05a72847 records each computed handle during the captured Configure. Once the caches are locked, DeltaStillHolds evaluates those handle programs again and takes the full path ('computed handle changed') when a value differs. Texture header writes and handle CB binds/writes still end reuse.
ideas.expected_saving_ms: 0.1-0.3 ms/frame. r50: 1,432-4,188/s ≈ 30-90 draws/frame. Each saves ~3.5 us (4.55 minus ~1 us to evaluate the programs again): 0.1-0.3 ms. More at the water, where #1161 counted ~31,000/s.
ideas.evidence: From the commit: 'At Kokiri village's water they were about 31,000 full draws a second (4.0 us to prepare each, against 1.0 us for a delta draw)'.
ideas.sources: Upstream open PR #1161, commit e05a72847 (4 files, +92/-24).
ideas.correctness_risks: The handle programs read CB and SSBO memory: an input the re-evaluation misses gives wrong textures. Our handle tables (#354's 64 bases) must be inside what the recorded inputs cover. Use FAST_DRAW_VERIFY and DELTA_DESCRIPTORS_VERIFY at the water and in Castle Town.
ideas.how_to_measure: The ReportFastDraws 'pipelines without delta draws: computed handles' count should go to ~0, with a new 'computed handle changed' count. Delta rate up; verify mismatches 0.

ideas.title: Allow delta draws across an indexed/non-indexed change or a topology change within the same class
ideas.mechanism: TakeReusableDraw takes the full path when is_indexed or the topology differs (vk_rasterizer.cpp:474-478). ConfigureDelta already takes is_indexed and rebinds the index buffer (UpdateGraphicsBuffers(is_indexed) and BindHostGeometryBuffers, vk_graphics_pipeline.cpp:1181-1184). With EDS plus EDS2 the key holds only the topology class (fixed_pipeline_state.cpp:130-134), and UpdateDynamicStates sets the topology dynamically (vk_rasterizer.cpp:4458-4486). Relax the check: allow a different is_indexed, and a different topology when the key collapses topology classes and the class representative is the same. Indirect draws and inline index draws stay full.
ideas.expected_saving_ms: 0.1-0.16 ms/frame. 2,234-2,803/s ≈ 48-60 draws/frame; with ~50-60% being the relaxable kinds, 25-36 draws x 4.55 us.
ideas.evidence: Reasoned. The kind breakdown is unknown until idea 2 splits 'different kind'.
ideas.sources: Original.
ideas.correctness_risks: Primitive restart enable depends on the topology (IsPrimitiveRestartSupported, vk_rasterizer.cpp:253-272): it must be updated on the delta path too. Point size and the polygon offset LUT depend on the topology (fixed_pipeline_state.cpp:390-394). Allow only cases where those match, or take the full path.
ideas.how_to_measure: The 'different kind' count in ReportFastDraws, split by idea 2's counter. Verify-run mismatches 0.

ideas.title: Later option: EDS3 blending, with blend enable and clip control as draw parameters
ideas.mechanism: Under the owner's EDS2 setting (settings.h:823-832; vulkan_device.cpp:742-768), blend state and depth clamp are in the pipeline key (fixed_pipeline_state.cpp:256, 279). So blend.enable[2] (0x4da), blend_per_target and viewport_clip_control writes are real pipeline changes. With dyna_state EDS3, and if the RX 9070 XT driver exposes extendedDynamicState3ColorBlendEnable, ColorBlendEquation, ColorWriteMask and DepthClampEnable (vulkan_device.cpp:1689-1699), these become dynamic state. UpdateBlending (vk_rasterizer.cpp:4528-4531) then sets them on both paths, so they can be fast-draw parameters gated by g_dynamic_blend. The pipeline count also drops.
ideas.expected_saving_ms: 0.3-0.5 ms/frame. ~5.5-7.5k/s last breaks ≈ 120-160 draws/frame x 4.55 us x 50-70%.
ideas.evidence: Reasoned. Whether the AMD Windows driver exposes these EDS3 features is not in the r50 log.
ideas.sources: Original. Follows the zone diagnosis's lever 3, which notes blend and clip control are key fields and must keep breaking unless the key excludes them.
ideas.correctness_risks: Changing dyna_state changes every pipeline key. The ~120k prepared pipelines were recorded with EDS2 keys, so check whether RecordedKeyForThisDevice remaps them or a full re-preparation runs; this must not break the preparation stamp. EDS3 blending on AMD drivers has a mixed history: check for wrong blending or alpha on water, the HUD and the FSR final pass. Owner decision; test only after ideas 1-3.
ideas.how_to_measure: A boot log line for the EDS3 feature bits. Then a run with dyna_state EDS3: 0x4da, 0x783 and 0x64f leave 'by last break', the pipeline count drops, and screenshots of water, HUD and transparency match through the debug server.

ideas.title: GPU page translation cache per thread (Eglantine b1e650849e by kraibse, via Fritchii EXP63 85a33019b)
ideas.zone: update buffers (0.5 us per draw), read handles, storage buffers, bank check (GpuToCpuAddress)
ideas.mechanism: Every draw re-resolves index and vertex buffer, UBO, SSBO and handle addresses through MemoryManager::GpuToCpuAddress (memory_manager.cpp:318-338). A small per-thread cache of 4 KiB page translations, tagged with the manager and map_serial (already bumped on remaps, memory_manager.cpp:172, 236), answers the repeats. Read the kill switch into a static once: Fritchii's port calls std::getenv on every lookup (85a33019b, line 48 of the diff).
ideas.expected_saving_ms: 0.1-0.4 ms/frame. kraibse measured the back thread 13.64 -> 13.25 ms/frame (-0.39) in OoT Kokiri. Our lookup is already two table reads, so expect less.
ideas.evidence: kraibse's measurement, quoted in the Fritchii commit message.
ideas.sources: Eglantine b1e650849e (kraibse); Fritchii EXP63 85a33019b (default off there).
ideas.correctness_risks: Every remap path must bump map_serial (PageTableOp/BigPageTableOp), or a stale translation reads the wrong memory. Cache only translations that pass our device-space check, as Fritchii does.
ideas.how_to_measure: EDEN_NX2_GPU_PROFILE=1 A/B at Kokiri: the ms per call of update buffers, read handles, storage buffers and bank check, and 'prepare us per draw' for both paths. EDEN_NX2_READ_CHECK=1 must stay at 0 differences.

ideas.area: Uniform/storage buffer binds and uploads, push descriptors, fences (made and skipped), and the 'other' bucket on the split's back (tuned4 cd5482ece). Three corrections to the phase-1 premises. (1) Upstream #1059 is already in tuned4 as 81ee8c090. BindSmallUniformReusing compares in place through GetSpan (uniform_stream_reuse.h:113-128), so porting it saves nothing more. (2) DevicePageFlags::Take already does a plain load before the RMW (gpu_dirty_memory_manager.h:240-250), and the bank snapshot map is already boost::unordered_node_map (buffer_cache_base.h:570-572, Fritchii 8b7bb3fab). (3) The fence counts were misread. The Fence zone's count covers every SignalFence call, skipped ones included. r50 L2549 shows 9,509 calls/s, of which 5,302 were skipped. 'Fence decisions/s' shows 3.7-5.6k fences made/s (delayed 1.3-3.0k, committed flushes 1.0-3.0k) and 5-11k skipped. So each made fence costs about 6-8 us exclusive, not 2.5 us. Example for L2549: 36.1 ms − 9,509 × ~0.3 us of CommitCacheFlushes ≈ 33 ms over 4,207 made fences = 7.9 us. Other findings from the logs: - Nearly every queue submit comes from a delayed fence. 'Scheduler per second' shows 1.9-2.7k submits/s, against 2.2-2.8k delayed fences/s. Every delayed fence ends in SubmitDeferredWork, which calls Flush (fence_manager.h:139-142). - The stream buffer is in device-local memory over OCuLink ('Stream buffer: 128 MiB in memory type 2 (device-local)'). It takes 135-188 MiB/s of uploads in gameplay. - The back waits 17-82 ms/s on spin mutexes, with 200-300 sleeps/s. The fencing thread copies downloads into guest memory while it holds buffer_cache.mutex (fence_manager.h:321, buffer_cache.h:2264-2316). - 'Uniform keeps in 600 frames' shows 1.1-1.4 M kept against 5.0-8.5 M streamed. That is ~2.2k kept and ~10k streamed small UBO binds per frame, plus ~1.4k native-bank binds; uniform buffers 62-73 ms/s works out to ~100 ns per UBO. - Push descriptors cost ~50 ns per stage call (8.7-9.0 ms/s for 167-185k calls), and delta draws already replay them (vk_graphics_pipeline.cpp:1213-1222). Descriptor reuse is not worth targeting. Per-frame figures below assume ~47 fps (r50 gameplay), so 1 ms/s ≈ 0.021 ms per frame.

ideas.title: Measure first: split fence, uniform and lock time with a few TEST zones and the existing EDEN_NX2_GPU_PROFILE=2
ideas.zone: fence, fence skipped, uniform buffers, other, spin mutex contention
ideas.mechanism: Step 1 needs no build: one run with EDEN_NX2_GPU_PROFILE=2. Its fine counters give uniform rebinds, streamed, cached and other plus uniform bytes (nx2_profile.h:204-209; counted at buffer_cache.h:2786-2805), which shows how many of the ~10k streamed binds per frame copy bytes and how many bytes. Step 2 adds profile-only TEST zones: (a) 'fence submit' around SubmitDeferredWork and the Flush calls InnerFence::Queue and FlushCommands make inside SignalFence (fence_manager.h:131-142; vk_fence_manager.cpp:22-30; vk_rasterizer.cpp:3048-3058). (b) 'fence commit' around CommitCacheFlushes (fence_manager.h:379-396), which includes its two cache-lock waits. (c) 'stream copy' plus bytes around the copies into the mapped stream: uniform_stream_reuse.h:137, buffer_cache.h:2804-2805, and the root-table memcpy at 2620-2622. (d) On the fencing thread, the hold time of the buffer_cache.mutex block at fence_manager.h:320-325, with landings/s and the time spent in PendingCpuWriteRanges (buffer_cache.h:2303). (e) InvalidateGPUCache outcomes: flag clear, gathered empty, gathered writes. (f) 'deferred call' around the Kind::Call body (gpu_split.cpp:773-780) and 'idle hook' around the in-loop hook (gpu_split.cpp:873-877), which are what make up 'other'.
ideas.expected_saving_ms: 0 by itself. It decides between items 2-8, which together claim ~1.2-2.8 ms/frame, and it rules out spending effort on push descriptors (~0.2 ms/frame in total).
ideas.evidence: These four zones and 'other' cover ~4.5-5 ms/frame together, yet none has sub-zones. Fence 36-38 ms/s and fence skipped 12-17 ms/s (r50 L2549, L4861). Spin contention 17-82 ms/s. 'other' 109-129 ms/s. The made-fence cost of 6-8 us is derived, not measured.
ideas.sources: Original. It reuses the fine-zone mechanism from 7dca362343 (TEST: fine profile zones, EDEN_NX2_GPU_PROFILE=2).
ideas.how_to_measure: Run the owner's usual Kokiri/Castle Town route once with EDEN_NX2_GPU_PROFILE=2 on the current build. Then make one TEST build with the zones above and read the 'GPU back thread per second' and fine-counter lines. Profile-only code: it stays off unless the variable is set, so it can stay in nx2 as a diagnostic.
ideas.correctness_risks: None. Profile-only. Keep the zones' clock reads out of unprofiled play (the Scope enabled flag already does this).

ideas.title: Port upstream PR #1161's report and fence half (792e12a47) and #1099's synced-release skip (c9f775dd0 with c0b8b7b51)
ideas.zone: fence, method (query report fine zone), spin mutex contention
ideas.mechanism: Four parts of 792e12a47. (1) The report operation lambda shrinks to a 48-byte ReportOp so std::function holds it without allocating.
