Our capture at query_cache.h:318-321 is ~110 bytes, more than MSVC's 56-byte small buffer. It is also built for immediate reports and then thrown away (query_cache.h:318 before the branch at 395-431), so today every report allocates and frees once. (2) Fence operation lists are recycled through spare_operations instead of 'uncommitted_operations.reserve(64)' after each made fence (fence_manager.h:122-125). That is a 4 KiB allocation per made fence, freed on the fencing thread. (3) Free query ids move to a vector FIFO instead of std::deque<size_t> (query_stream.h:127-149). MSVC's deque allocates a block every two pushes. (4) MayBeReadBackPage: atomic first/last bounds of read_back_pages let a report skip the buffer_cache.mutex lock pair in RasterizerVulkan::NoteReportPending/FinishReport (vk_rasterizer.cpp:2630-2638) when its page can't be a read-back page. From #1099 c9f775dd0: synced payload releases are not noted as pending, which removes two lock pairs per such release. Adapt it to our report_noted at query_cache.h:316-317. Our lambda has no is_synced, so derive it. Take c0b8b7b51 with it.
ideas.expected_saving_ms: 0.15-0.3 ms/frame. Reports: ~1.2k report_semaphore.query per frame. 0x6c3/0x54c/0x556 together are 3.5k per frame, about a third each. At ~100-150 ns saved per report (one alloc/free plus half a deque block) that is 0.12-0.18 ms. Fence lists: 4.2-5.2k made fences/s × ~0.3 us = 1.3-1.6 ms/s ≈ 0.03 ms. Lock skips: ~2.5k delayed reports/s × 2 lock pairs ≈ 0.2 ms/s uncontended, more where the fencing thread holds the lock (see item 8). Total ~0.15-0.25 ms, up to 0.3 ms with avoided contention.
ideas.evidence: Author's text: 'a report per draw (Ocarina of Time's occlusion counts) allocated one each'; 'MSVC's deque of size_t allocated every two pushes'; 'a list grew from 64 operations at most fences: ~30 a fence at Ocarina of Time's water'. #1099: NoteReportPending 'would only take the buffer cache's lock twice for each of them, about 1,700 times a second in Ocarina of Time'. No timings were given. My numbers are estimates from typical Windows LFH allocation costs.
ideas.sources: upstream open PR #1161 commit 792e12a47 (reports/fences part only; its fast-draw part belongs to another area). upstream open PR #1099 commits c9f775dd0 and c0b8b7b51.
ideas.how_to_measure: Compare the fence zone ms/s and, under EDEN_NX2_GPU_PROFILE=2, the 'query report' fine zone ms/s before and after. Spin mutex contention on the back should not rise. Run EDEN_NX2_READ_CHECK=1 for a few minutes: 'Read download check' must stay 0. Check that white flashes on leaves and walls are still gone in Kokiri.
ideas.correctness_risks: Our report lambda has extra captures that #1161's ReportOp lacks: delayed_release and payload for Nx2SemaphoreWaiters::OnDelayedReleaseDone, plus the shadow/mirror state. They must fit in the 48 bytes, or be packed, without dropping the OnDelayedReleaseDone call. MayBeReadBackPage must publish its bounds under the buffer cache mutex at every insert into read_back_pages and on removal. A missed bound means a report that is not tracked against a read-back page, which brings back the stale-report white flashes. The fence-list recycle must clear the lists after running their operations.

ideas.title: Bank check: skip unflagged pages in bulk with three page bitsets (on top of our EXP9 port)
ideas.mechanism: CheckNativeBankPagesTracked (buffer_cache.h:2940-3020) does per-page work on every page of every 64 KiB bank bind. It calls GetPointer twice: once in the mapped-size loop (2954-2957) and again per page. It calls Take twice, does a try_emplace into the node map (2978), and runs the reason chain, even though ~89% of pages end up skipped. Mode 3 skips exactly when the page is known, not collected, not written, not flagged for recheck, not CPU-dirty and not hot. Keep three back-thread-only bitsets indexed by device page, plain u64 words since only the back touches them: known (a snapshot exists), recheck (snapshot.recheck) and hot (changed_frame within NativeBankHotFrames). For a bank, load the one or two words that cover its 16 pages. Form the candidate mask: ~known | recheck | hot | collected-word | written-word, where the last two come from a relaxed load of the global DevicePageFlags words. When any_cpu_dirty is false, run the per-page path only for set bits. Do the mapped-size check in the same pass. Clear a page's hot bit lazily when its snapshot shows the window has expired. Clear known when the map is cleared at 16,384 entries (2959-2961). Skipping stays exact: same pages compared, same changes found.
ideas.expected_saving_ms: 0.25-0.4 ms/frame. Bank check is 34-35 ms/s for 78-81k binds/s (r50 L2549/L4861), i.e. 0.43 us per bind, with 626-672k pages/s skipped and 70-78k compared. Rough split: hot memcmps ~60-70k/s × ~0.15 us ≈ 10 ms/s, which stays. Mapped-size pass 80k × 16 × ~5 ns ≈ 6 ms/s, which mostly goes. Skipped-page work ≈ the remaining 15-19 ms/s, of which ~80% goes. Saved ≈ 12-18 ms/s ≈ 0.25-0.4 ms/frame. Bank check falls from 0.7-0.8 to ~0.35-0.45 ms/frame.
ideas.evidence: 'Native bank check (mode 3, 10 s)' lines from r50: 578k-871k binds and 4.7-7.0 M skipped per 10 s. Compared/changed: hot 523k-718k / 101-238, CPU-modified 34k-88k / 4.9k-10k, collected 8k-13.5k / 5.9k-9.8k, recheck 7k-12k / 0. The snapshot map is already a node map (buffer_cache_base.h:570-572), so the gain comes from skipping work, not from a faster map.
ideas.sources: Original. Builds on Fritchii EXP9 (9e8cb73ed, 1a64fe500 as ported in 7864fd62e/78b9e52d8) and Fritchii 8b7bb3fab. Upstream #1131 (1d8e4e2db, XXH3 skip of the once-a-frame bank re-upload) does not apply: EXP9 mode 3 removed the code it patches.
ideas.how_to_measure: For an A/B, temporarily keep the old loop behind a TEST switch. On the same route the 'Native bank check' line's binds, skipped and per-reason compared/changed counts must match the old code's rates. Run LICHII_BANK_CHECK=2 once: 'missed 0' must hold. Bank check ms/s in 'GPU back thread per second' should drop from ~34 to ~17-22 ms/s. Optional follow-up: log a histogram of frames since the previous change for hot-found changes. Hot compares are 52-72k/s for 10-24 real changes/s with NativeBankHotFrames = 120 (buffer_cache_base.h:574). If all hot-found changes come within a few frames, a shorter window would cut most of the remaining ~10 ms/s. That part carries a correctness risk and needs mode 2 to verify it.
ideas.correctness_risks: The bitsets must mirror the snapshot state exactly. Set known on insert and clear it with the map. Keep recheck in step with the std::exchange at 2985. Set hot whenever changed_frame is set. A missed bit means a skipped compare, i.e. a stale constant-buffer page: the Ocarina white flashes EXP9 fixed. Read the global page flags before the guest page, as Take does today.

ideas.title: Batch the submits that delayed (fence-flagged report) fences force, and drop the flush after queueing (#1161 58144d258)
ideas.zone: fence (also render pass count, Vulkan worker queue submit)
ideas.mechanism: With delay_fence set, SignalFence ends with SubmitDeferredWork, which calls Scheduler::FlushDeferred (fence_manager.h:139-142; vk_fence_manager.cpp:76-80). That submits whatever InnerFence::Queue or FlushCommands deferred through DeferFlush (vk_scheduler.cpp:256-275), so every fence-flagged short-query release costs a full submit. Each submit does EndRenderPass, CounterClose, InvalidateState and DispatchWork on the back (vk_scheduler.cpp:919-1000). It also resets the uniform reuse slots' tick, and the next draw re-emits all dynamic state. The change: for a delayed fence whose tick was deferred, don't submit at once. The fencing thread already asks for the submit when it reaches the fence: InnerFence::Wait, then Scheduler::WaitSubmitted, then RequestIdleHook (vk_fence_manager.cpp:39-52), which the back serves after its current Execute call (gpu_split.cpp:873-877). The idle hook (840-842) and the 500 us DeferFlush interval cover the rest. So the submit happens when someone needs it, and fences that arrive while the fencing thread waits on earlier GPU work share one submission. Safer refinement: keep the immediate submit when Nx2SemaphoreWaiters has registered waiters (count != 0; nx2.h:519ff), and have a waiter that registers later call RequestIdleHook. Also take #1161's 58144d258: drop the 'if (should_flush) rasterizer.FlushCommands()' after QueueFence (fence_manager.h:132-134).
ideas.expected_saving_ms: 0.12-0.25 ms/frame on the back, plus GPU time. Submits: 1.9-2.7k/s against 1.3-3.0k delayed fences/s, so ~45-55 submits per frame are forced. If batching halves them (~1.1k/s fewer) at ~5-10 us of back time each, that saves 5.5-11 ms/s = 0.12-0.23 ms/frame. Upper bound: made fences cost ~6-8 us exclusive, so ~0.4-0.55 ms/frame of the fence zone is submit-related if the delayed half carries most of it. The GPU gains fewer render-pass breaks: 4.4-6.3k render passes/s, each with attachment store and load at 1440p. 58144d258 alone: only 4-30 empty flushes/s are measured, so its own gain is small.
ideas.evidence: r50 'Scheduler per second: 2203 submits, 5209 render passes ... 6 flushes with nothing recorded'. 'Fence decisions/s: 5240 made (delayed fences 2817, committed flushes 2246 ...)'. Vulkan worker 'queue submit 43.9 ms (2213/s)'. DeferFlush's own note: batching fence submits within 500 us gave ~10-15% more fps in Hyrule Warriors.
ideas.sources: Original (the batching), using upstream's DeferFlush and WaitSubmitted machinery. Upstream open PR #1161 commit 58144d258 (cherry-pick of upstream 5b6fd59ff / Citron 3a3297553) for the double flush. Fritchii keeps the immediate submit with a comment about a 24 s hang (frizti/oot-gather-fix fence_manager.h, SignalFence), so vet against it.
ideas.how_to_measure: Compare submits/s and render passes/s in the 'Scheduler per second' line, the fence zone ms/s (with the 'fence submit' zone from item 1), and 'finishes waiting'. Watch the frame-time 1% lows and the front's acquire and writer waits: they must not rise. Test with GPU accuracy switched to High while the game runs (Fritchii's hang case), during scene loads, and with the EDEN_NX2_SPLIT_CHECK=1 build. Watch for 'Waited N s for the GPU thread to submit tick' warnings (vk_scheduler.cpp:298ff).
ideas.correctness_risks: No stale data. The risk is a stall: a delayed fence's operation runs only after its submit. If the back blocks inside one entry on that operation's result and never reaches the hook check, this deadlocks; Fritchii saw a 24 s wait. Also latency: a guest CPU polling the released value unregistered sees it later, but no later than the fencing thread's own request. Keep the immediate submit in WaitPendingFences (fence_manager.h:184).

ideas.title: Stream buffer in host memory over OCuLink: extend upstream PR #1156's placement rule to a slow link
ideas.zone: uniform buffers, update buffers, compute, texture upload (all copies into the stream buffer)
ideas.mechanism: Every small UBO streamed (uniform_stream_reuse.h:136-137; buffer_cache.h:2804-2805) and every stream-path upload writes into the 128 MiB stream buffer. That buffer is created as MemoryUsage::Stream (DEVICE_LOCAL|HOST_VISIBLE, vk_staging_buffer_pool.cpp:117; vulkan_memory_allocator.cpp:70-73), so with ReBAR the CPU's write-combined stores cross the PCIe 4.0 x4 OCuLink link, and the back's memcpy is limited by link throughput. #1156 (3ae157d3dc, made unconditional in 30c92c28e6) moves the stream buffer to host memory (MemoryUsage::Upload) only when the BAR window is 256 MiB or less. Our card has full ReBAR, so the rule keeps video memory. Extend StreamBufferInHostMemory with a measured rule: time a 4-8 MiB memcpy into the mapped stream buffer against host memory at startup, and choose host when the device write rate is below a threshold (e.g. under 8 GB/s). A rule based on the PCIe link width would also work.
ideas.expected_saving_ms: 0.4-0.7 ms/frame on the back, if the A/B confirms the bandwidth. Stream traffic is 135-188 MiB/s in gameplay (r49/r50 'Staging traffic per second'), i.e. 2.9-4.0 MiB/frame at 47 fps. At ~4-6 GB/s for WC writes over Gen4 x4, 3.5 MiB takes 0.6-0.9 ms. Host memory at 20-28 GB/s (#1156 measured 25-28) takes 0.13-0.18 ms. Difference ≈ 0.45-0.7 ms/frame, spread over the uniform buffers, update buffers and compute zones. If the measured device write rate turns out above ~10 GB/s, the gain falls to ≤0.2 ms and the idea should be dropped.
ideas.evidence: r49/r50 logs: 'Stream buffer: 128 MiB in memory type 2 (device-local)' at 15.2 s; stream traffic 107-188 MiB/s. #1156 on a GTX 1650 (small BAR, PCIe 3.0 x8): 255 ms/s copying into BAR memory at 0.8-1.0 GB/s against 25-28 GB/s to host; recording thread 36.7 to 22.3 ms/frame; GPU busy 26.9 to 30.3 ms/frame. Our link is faster than that window, so the gain is smaller; the 4-6 GB/s for our link is an estimate.
ideas.sources: upstream open PR #1156 commits 3ae157d3dc, 390385c94c and 30c92c28e6 (morrocoy-labs). The OCuLink/bandwidth rule is our extension.
ideas.how_to_measure: First get the stream copy rate from item 1's 'stream copy' zone and bytes. Then make a candidate build with 3ae157d3dc's EDEN_NX2_STREAM_IN_HOST=1 switch (experiment only; per policy it does not merge) and A/B on the same route. Back thread uniform buffers, update buffers and compute ms/s, plus total busy per frame, should drop. GPU frame time must not rise past the 16.7 ms budget with FSR 4 and frame generation on; check the sampled GPU time from the round-8 split and the EDEN_DKB_FRAME_TRACE fence timing. The 'Stream buffer:' log line confirms the placement.
ideas.correctness_risks: None for data: the same bytes go to a different memory type. The risk is performance. The GPU then reads UBOs, indices and storage data across the x4 link: #1156 saw GPU busy +13%, and for us GPU headroom with FSR 4, frame generation and 4K output decides whether it helps. Keep CheezyEmu's FSR 4 and frame-generation resources in their own allocations; the stream buffer does not hold them.

ideas.title: Shorten the fencing thread's buffer_cache.mutex hold during download landing
ideas.zone: spin mutex contention on the back (shows up inside the uniform buffers, draw, fence and flush work zones)
ideas.mechanism: ReleaseThreadFunc runs buffer_cache.PopAsyncFlushes under buffer_cache.mutex (fence_manager.h:320-325). Inside, PopAsyncBuffers (buffer_cache.h:2264-2316) writes the downloaded bytes into guest memory (WriteBlockUnsafe, 2250/2259; 30-256 MiB/s). For every landing group it also builds PendingCpuWriteRanges (2303), a gather over all 7 dirty-memory managers through std::function into a fresh RangeSet. Meanwhile the back spins and then sleeps on the same lock (SpinRecursiveMutex, spin_recursive_mutex.h:39ff). Two options. (a) Take one pending-write snapshot per fence plus a per-manager collect sequence number, so each landing re-gathers only writes collected after the snapshot instead of all of them. (b) Two phases: under the lock, compute the (device range, source pointer) list from `ranges` and do the gpu_modified_ranges.Subtract. Outside the lock, inside each DownloadLanding, do the copies, which keeps the landing protocol (rasterizer_download_area.h:56-120). Do (b) only if item 1's hold-time zone shows the copies dominate.
ideas.expected_saving_ms: 0.2-0.8 ms/frame if this thread is the main holder. The back's contention is 17-82 ms/s (r50 L2549: 843/s, 69.8 ms/s, 302 sleeps/s) = 0.35-1.7 ms/frame of in-zone waiting. Halving the fencing thread's share, assumed 50-100% of it, recovers 0.2-0.8 ms/frame. Wake latency after a sleep (200-300/s) is part of that cost.
ideas.evidence: Measured contention and sleep counts above. Downloads are 30-40 MiB/s in normal play and 210-256 MiB/s in r50's later windows ('buffer downloads 255910 KiB in 21565 copies'), all landed under the lock on the fencing thread. The only spin mutexes are the buffer and texture cache mutexes. The share this thread holds is an inference until item 1(d) measures it.
ideas.sources: Original. The landing protocol is upstream's/ours (DownloadLanding, #1028-era read-back work). EXP28's fence trims in Fritchii (4875a28bc) touch the same path but were reverted by Fritchii.
ideas.how_to_measure: Item 1(d) first: the fencing thread's buffer-lock hold in ms/s against the back's 'spin mutex contention: this thread' in the same 10 s windows. After the change, the back's contention ms/s and sleeps/s should fall, and the uniform buffers, draw and fence zones with them. Run EDEN_NX2_READ_CHECK=1 (differences must stay 0) and watch the 'held by download landings' count in the rasterizer-path writes line.
ideas.correctness_risks: High care needed. The download landing must still see every CPU write collected before it opened, and a write collected inside it must still Await. Otherwise GPU bytes overwrite newer CPU bytes: stale data and the white-flash class of bugs. Option (b) also changes when gpu_modified_ranges stops covering the range relative to the copy: a guest read trap between them must not read pre-copy memory. Keep the trap or read-download path ordered behind the copy.

ideas.title: Skip CommitCacheFlushes' two cache locks when neither cache has anything to commit
ideas.mechanism: Every SignalFence (9.5-14k/s) locks texture_cache.mutex and then buffer_cache.mutex just to ask HasUncommittedFlushes/HasAsyncFlushWork (fence_manager.h:379-396; texture_cache.h:2327-2334; buffer_cache.h:2087-2089). It does this even for the 5-9k/s fences then skipped as empty. If the fencing thread is landing downloads at that moment, the back waits behind it. Keep two std::atomic<bool> 'has uncommitted' flags, set and cleared under each cache's lock wherever uncommitted_downloads, uncommitted_async_buffers, uncommitted_gpu_modified_ranges and committed_gpu_modified_ranges change. CommitCacheFlushes reads the flags first and takes a lock only for a cache whose flag is set.
ideas.expected_saving_ms: 0.05-0.3 ms/frame. Uncontended: ~2 lock pairs × 9.5-14k/s × ~30 ns ≈ 0.6-0.8 ms/s ≈ 0.015 ms/frame. The real gain is the contended waits avoided. If fence commits account for 10-20% of the back's 17-82 ms/s spin waits, that is 2-16 ms/s ≈ 0.04-0.3 ms/frame. Item 1(b) gives the actual number.
ideas.evidence: Fence zone 36-38 ms/s and fence skipped 12-17 ms/s (r50). Committed flushes happen on 1.0-3.0k of the 9.5-14k fences/s ('Fence decisions/s'), so most calls find nothing to commit.
ideas.sources: Original. It follows the pattern of upstream's lock-free MustFlushRegion pre-check (vk_rasterizer.cpp:2640-2645) and #1161's MayBeReadBackPage.
ideas.how_to_measure: Item 1(b)'s 'fence commit' zone before and after, plus the back's spin contention. 'Fence decisions/s' must keep the same proportions: no fence with committed flushes may turn into a skipped one.
ideas.correctness_risks: A flag that misses a site that adds uncommitted work makes a fence skip its downloads, so the guest reads stale GPU-written memory. Audit every writer of the four containers, including off-back writers such as read traps and async read-back, and set the flag inside the same lock. EDEN_NX2_READ_CHECK=1 must stay at 0.

ideas.title: Small quick wins: InvalidateGPUCache early-out and hot-path function statics as plain flags
ideas.mechanism: (1) GPU::Impl::InvalidateGPUCache (gpu.cpp:117-147) always builds a std::function, takes applying_writes_mutex and gathers 7 dirty-memory managers, two std::mutex each (gpu_dirty_memory_manager.h:73-89; core.cpp:807-811). Return at once when !Core::g_writes_collected, as DmaPusher::ApplyCollectedWrites (dma_pusher.cpp:215-224) and AccelerateDMA (vk_rasterizer.cpp:4377) already do. Every Collect path sets the flag after its CAS (NoteCollected, gpu_dirty_memory_manager.h:151-156), and the flag is cleared before the gather (gpu.cpp:133), so an early return can't miss a write. (2) Function-local statics read on every UBO, buffer touch, report and flush cost a TLS epoch check each under the MSVC ABI, which clang-cl uses too. Examples: bank_check_mode (buffer_cache.h:2683), TouchBuffer's once_a_frame (buffer_cache.h:4216), CounterReport's two getenv statics (query_cache.h:251-255), and DeferFlush's interval (vk_scheduler.cpp:262). Make them plain inline globals read once, as #1059 did with g_uniform_stream_reuse (uniform_stream_reuse.h:36-50).
ideas.expected_saving_ms: 0.05-0.15 ms/frame together. (1) An empty gather costs ~0.3-0.5 us. Guest cores collect ~25-30k new page entries/s ('rasterizer-path writes by core ... collected' ≈ 250-300k per window), against 13-15k InvalidateGPUCache calls/s from fences alone. So the flag is often set, and maybe 20-40% of calls return early: ~3-6k/s × 0.4 us ≈ 1.2-2.4 ms/s ≈ 0.03-0.05 ms/frame. (2) ~2 ns × (~14k UBO binds + ~20k touches + ~1.2k reports + ~0.1k flushes) per frame ≈ 0.07 ms/frame.
ideas.evidence: Fence skipped costs 1.9-2.2 us each (r50: 11.6 ms/5,302 and 16.8 ms/8,907), and InvalidateGPUCache is part of that. The comment in #1059 itself records the per-call cost of MSVC function statics.
ideas.sources: (1) Original; the same guard upstream uses in DmaPusher and AccelerateDMA. (2) The pattern of upstream #1059 (81ee8c090, in tuned4) and #1095. A later, riskier step: drop InvalidateGPUCache from skipped fences entirely, since EXP35 already applies collected writes at command lists, acquires and DMA (memory.cpp:73-88). Do that only after item 1(e)'s counters show how often a skipped fence's gather finds writes.
ideas.how_to_measure: Item 1(e)'s counters: calls with the flag clear, gathered empty, gathered with writes. Fence skipped ms/s before and after. No change in the 'Native bank check' compared/changed collected counts or in 'Uniform keeps' verify mismatches (EDEN_NX2_UBO_KEEP_VERIFY=1).
ideas.correctness_risks: (1) None if every collector goes through CollectInPage/NoteCollected, which the grep confirms: memory.cpp:1083 is the only Collect caller. (2) A switch that moves from a function static to a global must still be read after nx2_switches.txt loads (re-read in VideoCore::CreateGPU, as ReadUniformStreamReuseSwitch does), or the user's settings file stops taking effect.

Partly. The ~15 ms/frame target looks reachable in lighter gameplay, but not yet in the heaviest areas.

What the back actually spends per frame:
- The '18.4 / 21.3 ms busy' figures are wall time per game frame. Zones plus 'other' add up to wall time (nx2_profile.h:522-528), and split wait is included.
- Unprofiled CPU (DKB gpu_back_cpu_ms_per_frame) is about 15.6-19.7 ms in r49 and 19.8-21.5 ms in r50 at 38-46 fps. Unprofiled play is also about 1 ms lighter than the profiled zones suggest.
- Hitting 15 ms therefore means cutting about 1-4 ms in r49-type scenes and about 5-6.5 ms in r50's heavy windows (Castle Town, water).

What the ranked items can deliver:
- Builds A+B (do-first and do-later): about 3-5 ms after overlap. The fast-draw items overlap each other, and delta draws also shrink the uniform, bank-check and translation costs.
- About 1-1.8 ms of that rests on #1216 converting as estimated, which build A's break-mask counter will confirm or refute.
- That likely gets r49-type gameplay to about 13-15 ms. Heavy windows end up around 15-17 ms: close to 60 fps, but not a locked 60.

What the heavy windows would need beyond that:
- Closing them needs about 1-2 ms more from build C's structural items: pair blocks, the dispatch memo, delta-after-lookup and possibly the host-memory stream buffer. Each of those is unmeasured and medium risk.
- The pin_gpu_threads A/B could also help, at no cost.

Even if the back reaches 15 ms, a consistent 60 fps also requires:
- the 4-7 ms collector Finish hitches to go (1% lows);
- the GPU frame time with FSR 4 at 4K plus frame generation to fit in 16.7 ms;
- the front's writer waits to shrink as the back speeds up, which they should.

My expectation: two builds give a clear step up, from about 45-50 to about 52-58 fps in typical play. A locked 60 everywhere is plausible only if build A's measurements show the conversion and lock-contention gains at the upper end of the estimates. Treat it as uncertain until then.
